words.ex: He accepted the gift with a smile.
words.ex_cn: 他微笑着接受了这份礼物。
words.en: If you accept something that you have been offered, you say yes to it or agree to take it.

words.ex: His acceptance of the offer made everyone happy.
words.ex_cn: 他接受了这份提议，让大家都很高兴。
words.en: The act of agreeing to receive or undertake something offered.

words.tr: v. 完成；实现；达到；获得；
words.ex: He worked hard to achieve his goal.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以完成他的目标。
words.en: To achieve something means to reach a particular goal or result through effort, skill, or courage.

words.ex: He felt proud of his academic achievement.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的学业成就感到自豪。
words.en: An achievement is something which someone has succeeded in doing, especially after a lot of effort.

words.tr:
v. 行动；表现；演戏；
n. 行动；法令；
words.ex: He acted quickly to save the child.
words.ex_cn: 他迅速行动救了那个孩子。
words.en: To do something for a particular purpose or in a particular way; to behave in a particular way; to have an effect or influence on something; to perform a part in a play, film, etc.

words.ex: He is an actor in a famous movie.
words.ex_cn: 他是电影中的一名演员。
words.en: An actor is a person whose profession is acting on the stage, in films, or on television.

words.ex: The government took quick action to fix the problem.
words.ex_cn: 政府迅速采取行动解决问题。
words.en: The fact or process of doing something, typically to achieve an aim.

words.tr: adj. 活跃的；积极的；主动的；
words.ex: He is an active student in class.
words.ex_cn: 他在课堂上是一个活跃的学生。
words.en: Someone who is active moves around a lot or does a lot of things.

words.ex: He adds two and three to get five.
words.ex_cn: 他把二和三相加得到五。
words.en: To put something together with something else so as to increase the size, number, or amount.

words.ex: The addition of a new chair made the room more comfortable.
words.ex_cn: 增加一把新椅子让房间更舒适了。
words.en: An addition is something that is added to something else, often to improve it or make it larger.

words.ex: He adds sugar to his coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他把糖加到咖啡里。
words.en: To include or incorporate something into an existing whole.

words.ex: My teacher gave me good advice about studying.
words.ex_cn: 我的老师给了我关于学习的好建议。
words.en: If you give someone advice, you tell them what you think they should do in a particular situation.

words.ex: I advise you to eat more vegetables.
words.ex_cn: 我建议你多吃蔬菜。
words.en: If you advise someone to do something, you tell them what you think they should do.

words.ex: I often give advice to my friends.
words.ex_cn: 我经常向我的朋友提建议。

words.tr: v. 买得起；担负得起；有时间做；
words.ex: I can't afford a new car.
words.ex_cn: 我买不起一辆新车。
words.en: If you cannot afford something, you do not have enough money to pay for it.

words.ex: This phone is affordable for students.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机对学生来说价格合理。
words.en: If something is affordable, most people have enough money to buy it.

words.tr: 短语动词，表示有能力负担做某事的费用或时间，通常用于表达经济或时间上的承受能力，如：买得起做某事；抽得出时间做某事
words.ex: I cannot afford to buy a new car.
words.ex_cn: 我买不起一辆新车。
words.en: To have enough money or resources to pay for or do something.

words.tr: v. 负担不起；无法承担；买不起；抽不出（时间/金钱等）
words.ex: I can't afford a new phone.
words.ex_cn: 我买不起新手机。
words.en: To lack the financial means to purchase or obtain something; unable to pay for.

words.ex: I agree with you.
words.ex_cn: 我同意你的看法。
words.en: If people agree with each other about something, they have the same opinion about it or say that they have the same opinion.

words.ex: They signed an agreement to share the costs.
words.ex_cn: 他们签署了一份分担费用的协议。
words.en: An agreement is a formal decision about future action which is made by two or more people, groups, or organizations.

words.ex: I disagree with your opinion.
words.ex_cn: 我不同意你的观点。
words.en: If you disagree with someone or disagree with what they say, you do not accept that what they say is true or you do not accept that it is the correct thing to do.

words.tr: phrase. 同意某人；与某人意见一致
words.ex: I agree with him on this plan.
words.ex_cn: 我同意他的这个计划。
words.en: To share the same opinion as someone else.

words.tr: v. 允许；留出；给予；承认；
words.ex: My parents allow me to go out on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 我的父母允许我周末外出。
words.en: If someone is allowed to do something, it is all right for them to do it and they will not get into trouble.

words.ex: My parents allow me playing video games after homework.
words.ex_cn: 我父母允许我做完作业后玩电子游戏。
words.en: To permit or authorize a particular action or activity.

words.ex: My mom allows me to watch TV after homework.
words.ex_cn: 我妈妈允许我做完作业后看电视。
words.en: To permit someone to do something.

words.ex: He became angry when his phone broke.
words.ex_cn: 当他手机坏了时，他生气了。
words.en: Feeling or showing strong annoyance, displeasure, or hostility; full of anger.

words.ex: He shouted angrily at the driver.
words.ex_cn: 他生气地对司机大喊。
words.en: In a manner that shows anger or strong resentment.

words.ex: His anger grew when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个消息时，他的愤怒增加了。
words.en: A strong feeling of annoyance, displeasure, or hostility.

words.tr: phrase. 对某人生气；生某人的气
words.ex: My mom is angry with me for coming home late.
words.ex_cn: 我妈妈因为我回家晚而生我的气。
words.en: To feel or show anger towards a specific person.
Feeling or showing strong displeasure or hostility because of something.

words.ex: The sun appears in the sky at dawn.
words.ex_cn: 太阳在黎明时出现。
words.en: If someone or something appears, they come into sight or become noticeable.

words.tr: n. 外观；外表；出现；露面；
words.ex: The appearance of the house surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子的外观让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: The way that someone or something looks or the act of coming into view.

words.ex: The cat disappeared behind the house.
words.ex_cn: 猫从房子后面消失了。
words.en: If someone or something disappears, they go away or are taken away so that you cannot see them any more.

words.ex: He arrives at the station at 8 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 他早上8点到达车站。
words.en: To reach a place, especially at the end of a journey.

words.ex: The arrival of the train was delayed by 20 minutes.
words.ex_cn: 火车的到达晚了20分钟。
words.en: The act of coming to a place or the moment when something or someone arrives.

words.ex: She will arrive at the airport tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 她明天将到达机场。

words.ex: He loves to paint and study art.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢绘画和学习艺术。
words.en: Art consists of paintings, sculpture, and other pictures or objects which are created for people to look at and admire or think deeply about.

words.ex: The artist painted a beautiful landscape.
words.ex_cn: 这位艺术家画了一幅美丽的风景画。
words.en: An artist is someone who draws or paints pictures or creates sculptures as a job or hobby.

words.tr: v. 出席；参加；注意；照料；
words.ex: He will attend the meeting tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会出席会议。
words.en: To be present at an event, meeting, or function; to take care of or look after someone or something.

words.ex: His attendance at the meeting was mandatory.
words.ex_cn: 他必须出席这次会议。
words.en: The act of being present at a place or event.

words.tr: phrase. 参加会议；出席一个集会
words.ex: She will attend a meeting tomorrow to discuss the project.
words.ex_cn: 她明天将参加会议讨论这个项目。
words.en: To be present at a meeting or event.

words.ex: He avoids eating sugar to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他避免吃糖以保持健康。
words.en: If you avoid something, you take action in order to prevent it from happening to you.

words.tr: 短语动词. 避免做某事
words.ex: He avoids eating sugary snacks.
words.ex_cn: 他避免吃甜食。
words.en: To refrain from or prevent an action or activity.

words.ex: He stayed awake all night to finish his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他整晚醒着完成作业。
words.en: If you are awake, you are not sleeping. If you awake, you wake up.

words.tr: v. 醒来；唤起；“awake”的过去式
words.ex: He awoke early to catch the bus.
words.ex_cn: 他早早醒来赶公交车。
words.en: To wake up; to become conscious or aware of something.

words.ex: This is a basic math skill.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个基本的数学技能。
words.en: You use basic to describe things, activities, and principles that are very important or necessary, and on which others depend.

words.ex: He basically just wants to be left alone.
words.ex_cn: 他基本上只是想一个人待着。
words.en: You use basically to indicate that you are stating a fact or opinion in a simple, clear, or definite way.

words.tr:
v. 打；敲打；击败；
n. 一击；跳动；
words.ex: He beat the drum loudly.
words.ex_cn: 他用力敲打鼓。
words.en: To defeat someone in a game, competition, election, or battle; to hit someone or something many times with your hand, a stick, etc.

words.tr: adj. 被踩实的； v. “beat”的过去分词；
words.ex: The beaten path through the forest was easy to walk on.
words.ex_cn: 穿过森林的被踩实的小路很容易走。
words.en: If someone is beaten in a game, competition, election, or battle, they are defeated by their opponents.

words.ex: She is a beautiful girl.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个美丽的女孩。
words.en: Pleasing the senses or mind aesthetically.

words.ex: She danced beautifully at the party.
words.ex_cn: 她在派对上漂亮地跳舞。
words.en: In a way that is pleasing to the senses or mind aesthetically.

words.tr: n. 美；美的事物；美丽；美人；
words.ex: The beauty of the sunset amazed everyone.
words.ex_cn: 日落的美让所有人都惊叹。
words.en: Beauty is the quality of being pleasing, especially to look at, or someone or something that gives great pleasure, especially when you look at it.

words.ex: The caterpillar becomes a butterfly.
words.ex_cn: 毛毛虫变成蝴蝶。
words.en: To begin to be something or to develop into something.

words.tr: v. 变成；成为；变得；“become”的过去式；
words.ex: He became a teacher after graduation.
words.ex_cn: 他毕业后成为一名老师。
words.en: the past tense of 'become', which means to begin to be something

words.ex: He begins his homework after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚饭后开始做作业。
words.en: To start doing something; to take the first step into a process or activity.

words.tr: v. 开始；创建；“begin”的过去式；
words.ex: He began to walk to school.
words.ex_cn: 他开始走路去学校。
words.en: Began is the past tense of begin. To begin means to start doing something.

words.ex: The meeting has begun.
words.ex_cn: 会议已经开始了。
words.en: Past participle of begin: to start doing something.

words.tr: n. 开头；开端； v. 开始；着手；“begin”的现在分词；
words.ex: The beginning of the story is very exciting.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事的开头非常精彩。
words.en: The point in time or space at which something starts.

words.ex: I believe you are telling the truth.
words.ex_cn: 我相信你在说真话。
words.en: If you believe in something, you think that it is true, or that it exists.

words.ex: The story is believable.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事令人信服。
words.en: If something is believable, it seems possible, real, or true.

words.tr: adj. 难以相信的；难以置信的；
words.ex: The magic trick was unbelievable.
words.ex_cn: 那个魔术难以相信。
words.en: If you say that something is unbelievable, you are emphasizing that it is very good, impressive, intense, or extreme.

words.tr: phrase. 相信某人；信任某人
words.ex: I believe in my brother because he always keeps his promises.
words.ex_cn: 我相信我弟弟，因为他总是信守承诺。
words.en: To have confidence in someone's abilities or character.

words.tr:
v. 打破；打断；
n. 休息；中断；破裂；
words.ex: He broke the glass by accident.
words.ex_cn: 他不小心打破了玻璃。
words.en: If you break something, you cause it to separate into two or more pieces, often in a way that is irreparable.

words.tr: v. 打破；打断；“break”的过去式； adj. 破产的；身无分文的；
words.ex: He broke the glass by accident.
words.ex_cn: 他不小心打碎了玻璃。
words.en: If you are broke, you have no money.

words.tr: adj. 破损的；弄坏的； v. 打破；打断；“break”的过去分词；
words.ex: The broken cup lay on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 破了的杯子躺在地板上。
words.en: Damaged or shattered into pieces, typically as a result of force or impact.

words.tr:
v. 建筑；建造；逐步加强；
n. 体格；体形；
words.ex: They build a house near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 他们在湖边建了一所房子。
words.en: To construct something by putting parts or material together.

words.tr: v. 建筑；建造；“build”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: They built a house last year.
words.ex_cn: 他们去年建了一栋房子。
words.en: The past tense and past participle of 'build', meaning to construct something by putting parts or material together.

words.tr: n. 建筑物；楼房； v. 建筑；“build”的现在分词；
words.ex: The tall building has 20 floors.
words.ex_cn: 这栋高楼有20层。
words.en: A building is a structure that has a roof and walls and stands more or less permanently in one place.

words.ex: He is busy with his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他正忙于做作业。
words.en: If you are busy, you are working hard or giving your attention to a particular activity.

words.ex: She was overwhelmed by the busyness of her daily life.
words.ex_cn: 她被日常生活的忙碌压得喘不过气来。
words.en: The state of being busy or occupied with activities.

words.ex: He is busy doing his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他正忙于做作业。
words.en: To be occupied with a particular activity.

words.tr: 短语动词. 忙于做某事；专注于某事
words.ex: He is busy with his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他正忙于做作业。
words.en: to be occupied or engaged with a specific task or subject

words.tr:
v. 叫；打电话；
n. 打电话；
words.ex: He calls his dog every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上叫他的狗。
words.en: If you call someone, you telephone them. If you call someone a particular name or title, you give them that name or title. If you call a meeting, you arrange for it to take place. If you call for something, you demand that it should happen.

words.tr: v. 给某人打电话；称呼某人
words.en: Telephone or contact someone.

words.tr: phrase. 拜访；要求；呼吁；号召
words.ex: I will call on my grandma this weekend.
words.ex_cn: 这个周末我将去拜访我的奶奶。
words.en: To visit someone; to formally ask or request someone to do something.

words.tr:
n. 照料；谨慎；关心；
v. 关心；在意；在乎；
words.ex: The nurse gave the baby good care.
words.ex_cn: 护士给了婴儿很好的照料。
words.en: If you care about something, you feel that it is important and are concerned about it.

words.ex: Be careful when you cross the street.
words.ex_cn: 过马路时要小心。
words.en: If you are careful, you give serious attention to what you are doing, in order to avoid harm, damage, or mistakes.

words.ex: She carefully wrote down the instructions.
words.ex_cn: 她仔细地记下了说明。
words.en: In a way that gives a lot of attention to what you are doing so that you do not have an accident, make a mistake, or damage something.

words.ex: He cares about his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他在乎他的朋友们。
words.en: If you care about something, you feel that it is important and are concerned about it.

words.ex: He carries a bag to school every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天带一个包去学校。
words.en: To carry something means to move it while supporting it, especially in your hands or arms.

words.ex: They will carry out the experiment tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他们明天将进行这个实验。
words.en: To perform or complete a task, duty, or project.

words.tr:
v. 抓住；赶上；理解；得病；接住；
n. 接住；搭扣；
words.ex: He tried to catch the ball.
words.ex_cn: 他试图抓住球。
words.en: If you catch something or someone, you manage to get hold of them or stop them from moving, often after a chase or search.

words.tr: v. 抓住；赶上；“catch”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The boy caught a fish in the river.
words.ex_cn: 男孩在河里抓到了一条鱼。
words.en: Caught is the past tense and past participle of catch, which means to seize or capture something or someone.

words.tr: phrase. 赶上；逮捕并处罚；（麻烦事）缠上
words.ex: He needs to catch up with his classmates.
words.ex_cn: 他需要赶上他的同学。
words.en: To reach the same standard or level as someone or something else, especially after a period of lagging behind.

words.ex: He goes out without a coat and catches a cold.
words.ex_cn: 他出去时没穿外套，结果感冒了。
words.en: To become ill with a cold.

words.tr:
v. 导致；引起；
n. 原因；理由；事业；
words.ex: Smoking can cause lung disease.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟会导致肺癌。
words.en: The cause of something is what makes it happen or exist.

words.ex: He chooses coffee every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都选择喝咖啡。
words.en: To choose means to select someone or something from a group of possibilities.

words.ex: He chose the red shirt.
words.ex_cn: 他选择了红色的衬衫。
words.en: If you choose someone or something from several people or things that are available, you decide which person or thing you want to have.

words.tr: v. 选择；“choose”的过去分词； adj. 挑选出来的；
words.ex: He was chosen as the team captain.
words.ex_cn: 他被选为队长。
words.en: Having been selected as the best or most suitable.

words.ex: He made a choice to study hard.
words.ex_cn: 他选择努力学习。
words.en: If you have a choice, you can choose between two or more things.

words.tr:
adj. 洁净的；干净的；
v. 打扫；使干净；
words.ex: The kitchen is clean after she wiped the counters.
words.ex_cn: 她擦了台面后，厨房变得洁净了。
words.en: If something is clean, it is free from dirt, marks, or unwanted substances.

words.tr: n. 清洁工人；清洁工具； adj. 更洁净的；更干净的；“clean”的比较级；
words.ex: The cleaner sweeps the floor every morning.
words.ex_cn: 清洁工人每天早上扫地。
words.en: A cleaner is a person whose job is to clean a place or a substance used for cleaning.

words.tr: phrase. 打扫干净；收拾整洁
words.ex: They clean up the room every Saturday.
words.ex_cn: 他们每星期六打扫房间。
words.en: To make a place or thing clean and tidy by removing dirt, rubbish, or unwanted items.

words.tr:
adj. 清楚的；明确的；清晰的；清澈的；晴朗的；
v. 清空；清除；放晴；使明确；
adv. 清楚地；彻底地；
words.ex: The instructions are clear.
words.ex_cn: 这些说明很清楚。
words.en: Free from anything that marks or darkens; transparent; bright; not obscure or ambiguous; easily understood; free from guilt or blame.

words.ex: He explained the problem clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他清楚地解释了这个问题。
words.en: In a way that is easy to see, hear, read, or understand.

words.tr: phrase. 清理；澄清；解决；放晴
words.ex: He helped to clear up the toys after playtime.
words.ex_cn: 他帮忙在玩完后收拾玩具。
words.en: To remove things that are causing a mess or obstruction; to explain something that was unclear; for the weather to become fine.

words.tr:
adj. 接近的；亲密的；
adv. 紧挨地；接近地；
v. 关闭；
words.ex: They are close friends.
words.ex_cn: 他们是亲密的朋友。
words.en: To move so as to bar passage through something; to shut.

words.ex: He watched the game closely.
words.ex_cn: 他紧密地观看了比赛。
words.en: In a way that is very near in space or time; with little or no space or time in between.

words.ex: They communicate well with each other.
words.ex_cn: 他们彼此沟通得很好。
words.en: To communicate means to share or exchange information, news, or ideas, especially by speaking or writing.

words.ex: Good communication helps people understand each other.
words.ex_cn: 良好的交流有助于人们相互理解。
words.en: The imparting or exchanging of information by speaking, writing, or using some other medium.

words.tr: phrase. 与某人交流；与某人沟通
words.ex: I can communicate with my friend in English.
words.ex_cn: 我能用英语和我的朋友交流。
words.en: To exchange information or ideas with someone.

words.ex: He compare apples and oranges to see which is sweeter.
words.ex_cn: 他比较苹果和橙子，看看哪个更甜。
words.en: If you compare one thing with another, you consider the similarities and differences between them.

words.ex: The comparison of the two phones helped me decide.
words.ex_cn: 对这两部手机的比较帮助我做出了决定。
words.en: When you make a comparison, you consider two or more things and discover the differences or similarities between them.

words.ex: We can compare apples with oranges to see the differences.
words.ex_cn: 我们可以把苹果和橙子进行比较，看看有什么不同。
words.en: To examine or look for the difference between two or more things.

words.tr: phrase. 将...与...作比较；把...比作...
words.ex: We can compare the human brain to a computer.
words.ex_cn: 我们可以将人脑与计算机作比较。

words.tr:
adj. 完整的；完成的；
v. 完成；
words.ex: The book is complete with all chapters.
words.ex_cn: 这本书有所有章节，是完整的。
words.en: If you complete something, you finish doing, making, or producing it.

words.ex: He completely forgot his keys.
words.ex_cn: 他完全忘记了钥匙。
words.en: In a way that is whole or entire; to the fullest extent.

words.ex: The bridge connects the two cities.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥连接了两座城市。
words.en: If something or someone connects one thing to another, or if one thing connects to another, the two things are joined together.

words.ex: The connection between the two wires is loose.
words.ex_cn: 两根电线之间的连接松了。
words.en: A connection is a relationship between two things, people, or groups.

words.tr: v. 把...与...联系起来；与...有关
words.ex: We can connect the printer with the computer using a cable.
words.ex_cn: 我们可以用一根线缆将打印机和电脑连接起来。

words.ex: I consider going to the park tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我考虑明天去公园。
words.en: If you consider something, you think about it carefully.

words.ex: He gave careful consideration to his decision.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的决定进行了仔细考虑。
words.en: Consideration is the process of giving careful thought to something before making a decision or taking action. It also refers to the quality of being thoughtful towards the needs and feelings of others.

words.ex: He is considering doing yoga every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他正在考虑每天早上做瑜伽。
words.en: To think about or evaluate the possibility of performing a particular action.

words.ex: I consider him as a friend.
words.ex_cn: 我把他当作朋友。
words.en: To think about something in a particular way; to have a certain opinion.

words.ex: He will continue walking after the break.
words.ex_cn: 休息后他会继续走路。
words.en: If someone or something continues to do something, they keep doing it and do not stop.

words.ex: The continuation of the project depends on funding.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目的继续取决于资金。
words.en: The act of continuing something or the state of being continued.

words.ex: He continues doing his homework after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚饭后继续做作业。
words.en: To keep performing an activity or action without stopping.

words.ex: He continues to do his homework every night.
words.ex_cn: 他每天晚上继续做作业。
words.en: To keep doing something without stopping.

words.tr:
n. 控制；管制；
v. 控制；操纵；
words.ex: The teacher has good control of the class.
words.ex_cn: 老师对课堂有很好的控制。
words.en: To control something means to have power over it and to be able to make it do what you want.

words.tr: adj. 受控制的； v. 控制；“control”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The experiment was conducted in a controlled environment.
words.ex_cn: 这个实验是在受控制的环境中进行的。
words.en: If something is controlled, it is done or organized according to a particular method or system.

words.ex: The pilot must keep control of the plane.
words.ex_cn: 飞行员必须控制飞机。

words.ex: He creates beautiful paintings with colors.
words.ex_cn: 他用色彩创造美丽的画作。
words.en: To create means to bring something into existence or to cause something to happen as a result of one's actions.

words.ex: The painting is a beautiful creation of the artist.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画是艺术家的一个美丽作品。
words.en: The act or process of bringing something into existence.

words.ex: He is a creative boy who draws nice pictures.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个有创造力的男孩，会画漂亮的画。
words.en: Someone who is creative has the ability to invent and develop original ideas, especially in the arts.

words.tr:
v. 横过；穿过；交叉；
n. 十字架；十字形记号；
adj. 恼怒的；
words.ex: Please cross the street carefully.
words.ex_cn: 请小心横过街道。
words.en: To go from one side of something to the other; to place or lie across something else; to oppose.

words.tr:
prep. 穿过；横过；在…对面；
adv. 横过；穿过；越过；
words.ex: He walked across the street.
words.ex_cn: 他穿过街道。
words.en: From one side to the other of something with clear limits, such as an area of land, a road, or a river.

words.ex: A large crowd gathered at the square.
words.ex_cn: 一大群人聚集在广场上。
words.en: A crowd is a large group of people who have gathered together, for example, to watch or listen to something interesting, or to protest about something.

words.tr: adj. 拥挤的；密集的； v. “crowd”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The bus was crowded during rush hour.
words.ex_cn: 高峰时段公交车很拥挤。
words.en: If a place is crowded, it is full of people.

words.tr: 短语动词. 挤满了……；充满……
words.ex: The market is crowded with people on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 周末市场里挤满了人。
words.en: To be filled with a large number of people or things in a way that makes movement or access difficult.

words.tr:
v. 切；割；削减；
n. 切；割；削减；
words.ex: He cut the apple with a knife.
words.ex_cn: 他用刀切了苹果。
words.en: To make an opening, incision, or wound in (something) with a sharp-edged tool or object.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 切碎；使伤心；使难过
words.ex: He cut up the apple into small pieces.
words.ex_cn: 他把苹果切成了小块。
words.en: To cut something into pieces; to injure someone by making cuts in their skin; to upset someone emotionally.

words.ex: There is danger near the river.
words.ex_cn: 河边有危险。
words.en: Danger is the possibility that someone may be harmed or killed.

words.ex: The river is dangerous for children.
words.ex_cn: 这条河对孩子来说很危险。
words.en: If something is dangerous, it is able or likely to hurt or harm you.

words.ex: The child is in danger near the busy road.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在繁忙的马路旁很危险。
words.en: To be in a situation where harm or loss is possible.

words.tr:
adj. 黑暗的；暗色的；深色的；
n. 黑暗；夜；暗色；
words.ex: The room was dark after the power went out.
words.ex_cn: 停电后，房间变得黑暗。
words.en: The absence of light in a place is referred to as dark. It can also describe something that is not light in color, or something that is mysterious or difficult to understand.

words.ex: The darkness made it hard to see the path.
words.ex_cn: 黑暗使我看不清道路。
words.en: The absence of light in a place, making it difficult or impossible to see.

words.tr: adv. 漆黑地；黑暗地；险恶地；负面地
words.ex: She spoke darkly about her past.
words.ex_cn: 她含糊其辞地谈起了她的过去。
words.en: In a manner that is dark or obscure, either literally or metaphorically.

words.ex: He decides to go home early.
words.ex_cn: 他决定早点回家。
words.en: If you decide to do something, you choose to do it, usually after you have thought carefully about the other possibilities.

words.ex: He made a quick decision to leave.
words.ex_cn: 他迅速做出了离开的决定。
words.en: A decision is a choice that you make about something after thinking about it.

words.tr: 短语动词. 决定做某事
words.ex: He decided to do his homework after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他决定晚饭后做作业。
words.en: To make a choice or judgment about a course of action.

words.ex: The country is developing its economy.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家正在发展它的经济。
words.en: To develop means to grow or cause to grow and become more mature, advanced, or elaborate.

words.ex: The development of the town took many years.
words.ex_cn: 这个小镇的发展花了许多年。
words.en: Development is the process of growth, progress, or making something more advanced.

words.tr: v. 发展；发育；“develop”的现在分词； adj. 发展中的；
words.ex: The country is developing its economy.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家正在发展它的经济。
words.en: A developing country or area of the world is poorer and has less advanced industries, especially in Africa, Latin America, or Asia.

words.tr: v. 发展；发育；“develop”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 发达的；先进的；
words.ex: The country developed quickly after the war.
words.ex_cn: 战争后，这个国家迅速发展。
words.en: A developed country, industry, or system is advanced and has a lot of economic activity.

words.ex: It's important to develop a habit of reading every day.
words.ex_cn: 养成每天阅读的习惯很重要。
words.en: To develop a habit means to start doing something regularly until it becomes a usual part of your life.

words.ex: The old tree died last winter.
words.ex_cn: 那棵老树去年冬天死了。
words.en: To die means to stop living and become dead.

words.tr: v. 死亡，枯萎；死亡，枯萎（ die的过去式和过去分词 ）；
words.ex: The flowers died because of no water.
words.ex_cn: 这些花因为缺水而枯萎了。
words.en: If someone dies, they stop living. If something dies, it stops existing or functioning.

words.ex: His death made everyone very sad.
words.ex_cn: 他的去世让所有人都很难过。
words.en: The end of the life of a person or organism.

words.tr:
adj. 死的；
n. 死人；
adv. 完全地；
words.ex: The dead bird lay on the ground.
words.ex_cn: 那只死鸟躺在地上。
words.en: No longer alive; deprived of life.

words.ex: The two apples are different.
words.ex_cn: 这两个苹果不一样。
words.en: not the same as another or each other; unlike in nature, form, or quality

words.ex: There is a big difference between apples and oranges.
words.ex_cn: 苹果和橙子之间有很大的差异。
words.en: A difference is a way in which two or more things are not the same.

words.ex: This book is different from that one.
words.ex_cn: 这本书和那本书不一样。
words.en: To not be the same as something or someone else.

words.ex: This math problem is difficult.
words.ex_cn: 这道数学题很难。
words.en: Something that is difficult is not easy to do, understand, or deal with.

words.ex: He faced difficulty in solving the math problem.
words.ex_cn: 他在解决这道数学题时遇到了困难。
words.en: A difficulty is a problem or issue that is hard to deal with or understand.

words.ex: He walked difficultly through the deep snow.
words.ex_cn: 他艰难地穿过厚厚的雪地。
words.en: In a manner that is hard to do, achieve, or accomplish; not easily.

words.ex: He discovered a new planet last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年发现了一颗新行星。
words.en: If you discover something that you did not know about before, you become aware of it or find it.

words.ex: The discovery of penicillin saved millions of lives.
words.ex_cn: 青霉素的发现拯救了数百万人的生命。
words.en: The act of finding something that had not been known before.

words.ex: We will discuss the homework tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我们明天讨论作业。
words.en: To discuss something means to talk about it with someone and tell each other your ideas or opinions.

words.ex: We had a discussion about homework.
words.ex_cn: 我们进行了一次关于作业的讨论。
words.en: A discussion is a conversation or debate about a specific topic.

words.ex: Let's discuss the project tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我们明天讨论这个项目。

words.ex: We need to have a discussion about the project.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要就这个项目进行讨论。

words.ex: I do my homework every evening.
words.ex_cn: 我每天晚上做作业。
words.en: To perform or accomplish something

words.ex: He did his homework after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚饭后做了作业。
words.en: Did is the past tense of do.

words.tr: v. 完成；“do”的过去分词； adj. 已完成的；
words.ex: I done my homework.
words.ex_cn: 我完成了我的作业。
words.en: If something is done, it has been completed or finished.

words.ex: I draw money from the bank every week.
words.ex_cn: 我每周从银行提取钱。
words.en: To make a picture, pattern, or diagram by making lines and marks, especially with a pen or pencil, on paper.

words.tr: v. 画；提取；吸引；“draw”的过去式；
words.ex: He drew a cat on the paper.
words.ex_cn: 他在纸上画了一只猫。
words.en: Drew is the past tense of draw, which means to produce a picture or diagram by making lines and marks on paper or another surface.

words.tr: v. 吸引；"draw"的过去分词；画；拉；提取；“draw”的过去分词；
words.ex: The bright colors drawn the children's attention.
words.ex_cn: 鲜艳的颜色吸引了孩子们的注意。
words.en: If someone looks drawn, their face is thin and they look very tired, ill, worried, or unhappy.

words.tr: n. 图画；绘画；制图； v. 提取；吸引；画；“draw”的现在分词；
words.ex: The child made a drawing of a cat.
words.ex_cn: 孩子画了一幅猫的图画。
words.en: A drawing is a picture made with a pencil, pen, or crayon rather than paint.

words.tr:
v. 驾驶；驱使；
n. 动力；
words.ex: He drives a car to work every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天开车去上班。
words.en: To operate and control the direction and speed of a motor vehicle; to push, propel, or carry along forcibly or strongly.

words.tr: v. 驱使；驾驶；“drive”的过去式；
words.ex: Fear drove him to leave the city.
words.ex_cn: 恐惧驱使他离开了这座城市。
words.en: A drove is a large group of animals, especially cattle or sheep, moving together. As a verb, it is the past tense of drive, meaning to force animals or people to move in a particular direction.

words.tr: v. 驱使；驾驶；“drive”的过去分词； adj. 发愤图强的；
words.ex: Fear of failure drove him to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 对失败的恐惧驱使他更加努力工作。
words.en: If you describe someone as driven, you mean they are very strongly motivated to achieve something or to do something.

words.ex: The driver stopped the car at the red light.
words.ex_cn: 司机在红灯处停了车。
words.en: A driver is a person who drives a vehicle.

words.tr:
v. 落下；掉下；
n. 滴；下落；
words.ex: The apple dropped from the tree.
words.ex_cn: 苹果从树上落了下来。
words.en: If you drop something, you accidentally let it fall.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 顺便访问；顺道拜访
words.ex: I will drop by your house after work.
words.ex_cn: 我下班后会去你家拜访。
words.en: To visit someone casually and usually without having arranged it before.

words.ex: This math problem is easy.
words.ex_cn: 这道数学题很容易。
words.en: If a job or action is easy, you can do it without difficulty because it is not complicated and causes no problems.

words.ex: The easiness of the test made everyone happy.
words.ex_cn: 考试的简单让所有人都很高兴。
words.en: The quality of being easy to do or achieve; lack of difficulty.

words.ex: He can solve the problem easily.
words.ex_cn: 他很容易就能解决这个问题。
words.en: Without difficulty or effort.

words.tr:
adj. 困难的；坚硬的；费劲的；
adv. 努力地；
words.ex: This math problem is hard.
words.ex_cn: 这个数学题很难。
words.en: If something is hard, it is very difficult to do or deal with. It can also mean that something is solid and firm, not soft or liquid.

words.ex: They want to educate their children well.
words.ex_cn: 他们想好好教育自己的孩子。
words.en: To educate someone means to teach them over a period of time at a school, college, or university.

words.ex: He values education very much.
words.ex_cn: 他非常重视教育。
words.en: Education is the process of teaching and learning, especially in a school or college, or the knowledge that you get from this.

words.tr: adj. 教育的；有教育意义的；
words.ex: This is an educational video for children.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个为儿童制作的教育视频。
words.en: Educational means relating to education or the process of education.

words.ex: My teacher encourages me to speak English every day.
words.ex_cn: 我的老师鼓励我每天说英语。
words.en: If you encourage someone, you give them confidence, for example by letting them know that what they are doing is good and telling them that they should continue to do it.

words.ex: Her mother gave her encouragement before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 考试前，她妈妈给了她鼓励。
words.en: Encouragement is the act of giving someone support, confidence, or hope.

words.ex: My mom encourages me to study hard.
words.ex_cn: 我妈妈鼓励我努力学习。
words.en: To urge or persuade someone to perform a specific action.

words.ex: I enjoy eating ice cream on hot days.
words.ex_cn: 我喜欢在热天吃冰淇淋。
words.en: If you enjoy something, you find pleasure and satisfaction in doing it or experiencing it.

words.ex: The picnic was an enjoyable day with friends.
words.ex_cn: 野餐是和朋友一起度过的愉快一天。
words.en: Something that is enjoyable gives you pleasure.

words.tr: 短语. 喜欢做某事；享受做某事的过程
words.ex: He enjoys playing soccer after school.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢放学后踢足球。
words.en: To take pleasure in an activity or hobby.

words.ex: He enters the room quietly.
words.ex_cn: 他悄悄地进入房间。
words.en: To come or go into a place; to become involved in a situation or activity; to begin a particular period or stage; to record information in a book or computer.

words.ex: The entrance to the building is on the left.
words.ex_cn: 这座建筑的入口在左边。
words.en: An entrance is a way into a place, such as a door or gate. It can also refer to the act of entering a place or the right to enter.

words.ex: The kids get excited when they see the clown.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们看到小丑时会兴奋起来。
words.en: To excite someone means to cause them to feel very enthusiastic and eager.

words.tr: adj. 令人激动的；使人兴奋的； v. “excite”的现在分词；
words.ex: The football match was exciting.
words.ex_cn: 这场足球赛令人激动。
words.en: If something is exciting, it makes you feel very happy or enthusiastic.

words.tr: adj. 兴奋的； v. 使兴奋；使激动；“excite”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The children were excited about the party.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们对派对感到兴奋。
words.en: If you are excited, you are so happy that you cannot relax, usually because you are thinking about something pleasant that you are going to do or experience.

words.ex: The children felt excitement before the birthday party.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在生日派对前感到兴奋。
words.en: A feeling of great enthusiasm and eagerness.

words.ex: Can you explain this math problem?
words.ex_cn: 你能解释一下这个数学问题吗？
words.en: To make something clear or easy to understand by describing or giving information about it.

words.ex: He gave a simple explanation for his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的错误给出了一个简单的解释。
words.en: An explanation is a statement or account that makes something clear or provides a reason for something.

words.tr:
v. 表达；表示；
adj. 明确的；
n. 特快列车；快件服务；
words.ex: He can express his feelings clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他能清楚地表达自己的感受。
words.en: If you express an idea or feeling, or express yourself, you show what you think or feel.

words.ex: His expression showed he was happy.
words.ex_cn: 他的表情显示他很快乐。
words.en: The act of making your thoughts, feelings, etc., known by speech, writing, or some other method.

words.tr: phrase. 表达某人的感情；抒发某人的情感
words.ex: He can express his feelings through music.
words.ex_cn: 他可以通过音乐表达自己的感情。

words.tr: v. 无法做到；失败；不及格；倒闭；
words.ex: He failed to finish the race.
words.ex_cn: 他没能完成比赛。
words.en: If you fail to do something that you were trying to do, you are unable to do it or do not succeed in doing it.

words.ex: He felt sad after the failure of his business.
words.ex_cn: 他的生意失败后，他感到很难过。
words.en: The lack of success in achieving or doing something.

words.tr: phrase. 未能做某事；没有成功完成某事
words.ex: He fails to do his homework every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都未能完成作业。
words.en: If you fail to do something that you were trying to do, you are unable to do it or you do not succeed in doing it.

words.ex: He failed in the exam last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周考试不及格。

words.tr:
adj. 公平的；相当大的；合理的；
n. 集市；
words.ex: The teacher gave a fair grade to every student.
words.ex_cn: 老师给每个学生都给了一个公平的分数。
words.en: Fair means treating people equally without favouritism or discrimination.

words.ex: The movie was fairly interesting.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影相当地有趣。
words.en: To a moderately sufficient extent or degree.

words.ex: The teacher showed fairness in grading all students.
words.ex_cn: 老师在给所有学生评分时展现了公平。
words.en: Fairness is the quality of treating people equally or in a way that is right or reasonable.

words.tr: adj. 不公正的；不公平的；
words.ex: The teacher gave an unfair test.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了一个不公正的考试。
words.en: If you describe a situation or action as unfair, you mean that it is not right or reasonable, especially because it does not treat people equally.

words.tr:
v. 下降；跌倒；
n. 落下；跌落；秋天；
words.ex: The temperature falls quickly at night.
words.ex_cn: 夜晚温度迅速下降。
words.en: To move downward, typically rapidly and freely without control, from a higher to a lower level.

words.tr: v. 跌倒；下降；砍伐；“fall”的过去式；
words.ex: He fell off the bike.
words.ex_cn: 他从自行车上摔了下来。
words.en: To cut down (a tree); to knock down (a person or animal); the skin of an animal with the hair or wool still on it; fierce or cruel.

words.tr: v. 下降；跌倒；“fall”的过去分词； adj. 落下的；
words.ex: The leaf fallen from the tree.
words.ex_cn: 叶子从树上落了下来。
words.en: Having dropped or come down from a higher place, often used to describe leaves, snow, or someone's moral state.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 跌倒；倒塌；失败
words.ex: The boy fell down from the chair.
words.ex_cn: 男孩从椅子上摔了下来。
words.en: To fall down means to move from a higher to a lower position, typically rapidly and without control, often resulting in landing on the ground.

words.ex: He falls in love with her when he sees her smile.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到她的微笑时，他就爱上了她。
words.en: To begin to feel romantic love for someone.

words.tr:
adv. 迅速；
adj. 快的；迅速的；
words.ex: He runs fast.
words.ex_cn: 他跑得很快。
words.en: Moving or capable of moving at high speed.

words.ex: He runs faster than his brother.
words.ex_cn: 他跑得比他弟弟快。
words.en: Comparative of fast: moving or capable of moving at high speed.

words.tr: adj. 快的( fast的最高级 )；
words.ex: He is the fastest runner in the school.
words.ex_cn: 他是学校里跑得最快的人。
words.en: Superlative form of fast, meaning moving or capable of moving at high speed.

words.tr:
n. 害怕；惧怕；
v. 害怕；惧怕；
words.ex: He felt a deep fear when he saw the snake.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到蛇时，感到深深的害怕。
words.en: An unpleasant emotion caused by the threat of danger, pain, or harm.

words.ex: The child was fearful of the dark.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子害怕黑暗。
words.en: If you are fearful of something, you are afraid of it.

words.ex: I fear to speak in public.
words.ex_cn: 我害怕在公众面前讲话。

words.tr: phrase. 害怕做某事；担心做某事会带来不好的结果
words.ex: He is afraid of making mistakes in class.
words.ex_cn: 他害怕在课堂上犯错。
words.en: To feel fear regarding the possibility of performing a specific action.

words.tr:
v. 喂；吃；
n. 饲养；喂养；
words.ex: She feeds the cat every morning.
words.ex_cn: 她每天早上喂猫。
words.en: To give food to a person or an animal; to supply something to a machine or a system.

words.tr: v. 喂；吃；“feed”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: She fed the cat every morning.
words.ex_cn: 她每天早上喂猫。
words.en: To provide food for someone or something, or to give someone or something the necessary materials or resources for a particular purpose.

words.ex: Wolves feed on deer in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 狼在森林里以鹿为食。
words.en: To consume something as food or to derive nourishment from it.

words.tr:
v. 感到；认为；触摸；
n. 感受；
words.ex: I feel happy today.
words.ex_cn: 我今天感到开心。
words.en: To experience a sensation or emotion through touch or perception.

words.tr: v. 感到；认为；“feel”的过去式和过去分词； n. 毛毡；毡制品；
words.ex: I felt happy when I saw my friend.
words.ex_cn: 当我见到我的朋友时，我感到开心。
words.en: If you feel a particular emotion or physical sensation, you experience it.

words.tr: n. 感觉； v. 感到；“feel”的现在分词；
words.ex: I have a feeling it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我感觉明天会下雨。
words.en: An emotion or a physical sensation.

words.tr:
v. 打架；战斗；
n. 打架；战斗；
words.ex: The two boys fight every day after school.
words.ex_cn: 这两个男孩每天放学后都打架。
words.en: To fight means to take part in a violent struggle involving the exchange of physical blows or the use of weapons. It can also refer to a determined effort to achieve or resist something.

words.tr: v. 战斗；打架；争论；“fight”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: They fought in the war last year.
words.ex_cn: 他们去年在战争中战斗。
words.en: Fought is the past tense and past participle of fight. To fight means to take part in a violent struggle involving the exchange of physical blows or the use of weapons.

words.ex: He fills the bottle with water.
words.ex_cn: 他把瓶子装满水。
words.en: To make or become full; to put something into a container or space so that it is completely or almost completely full.

words.ex: He fills the bottle with water.
words.ex_cn: 他把瓶子装满水。
words.en: To make or become full.

words.ex: The room is filled with laughter.
words.ex_cn: 房间里充满了笑声。
words.en: To have a lot of a particular quality or thing.

words.tr: v. 找到；发现；感到；认为；
words.ex: I found my keys under the table.
words.ex_cn: 我在桌子下面找到了我的钥匙。
words.en: If you find someone or something, you see them or learn where they are, either by chance or because you have been looking for them.

words.tr: v. 发现；找到；建立；认为；“find”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He found a strange stone on the beach.
words.ex_cn: 他在海滩上发现了一块奇怪的石头。
words.en: To establish or set up (an organization, institution, or place) on a firm or permanent basis.

words.ex: I want to find out why he is late.
words.ex_cn: 我想弄清楚他为什么迟到。
words.en: To discover a fact or piece of information, often by making an effort to do so.

words.ex: He will finish his homework before dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他会在晚饭前完成作业。
words.en: To finish something means to reach the end of it or to complete it.

words.tr: 短语动词. 完成做某事
words.ex: He finished doing his homework before dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他在晚饭前完成了作业。
words.en: Complete an activity or task.

words.tr:
v. 符合；合身；
adj. 健康的；适合的；
words.ex: This shirt fits me well.
words.ex_cn: 这件衬衫很合我的身。
words.en: If something fits, it is the right size and shape to go onto a person's body or onto a particular object.

words.tr: n. 装配工；试衣裁缝，地毯安装工；（服装或鞋子的）质检员; adj. 更健壮的；更适合的；更能胜任...
words.ex: He works as a fitter in the factory.
words.ex_cn: 他在工厂里做装配工。
words.en: A fitter is a person whose job is to put together, adjust, or repair machinery or equipment. As a verb, to fit means to be the right size or shape for someone or something.

words.tr: phrase. 适合的；胜任的；符合条件的
words.ex: This water is not fit for drinking.
words.ex_cn: 这水不适合饮用。
words.en: Suitable or appropriate for a particular purpose or person.

words.ex: He runs every morning to keep fit.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上跑步以保持健康。
words.en: To maintain one's health and physical condition through regular exercise and a healthy diet.

words.tr:
v. 飞翔；飞行；
n. 苍蝇；
words.ex: Birds fly in the sky.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿在天空中飞翔。
words.en: To move through the air using wings; or a small insect with two wings.

words.tr: v. 飞翔；飞行；“fly”的过去式；
words.ex: The bird flew over the tree.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿飞过了树。
words.en: Flew is the past tense of fly, which means to move through the air using wings.

words.tr: v. 飞；坐飞机；“fly”的过去分词；
words.ex: The bird has flown away.
words.ex_cn: 这只鸟已经飞走了。
words.en: Flown is the past participle of fly, meaning to move through the air using wings.

words.tr: n. 航班；飞行；（阶梯的）一段；
words.ex: The flight to Beijing leaves at 8 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 飞往北京的航班早上8点起飞。
words.en: A flight is a journey made by flying, usually in an aircraft.

words.ex: The dog follows its owner every day.
words.ex_cn: 狗每天跟随它的主人。
words.en: To go or come after (a person or thing proceeding ahead); move or travel behind.

words.tr: phrase. 遵守规则；按照规定行事
words.ex: It's important to follow the rules to maintain order.
words.ex_cn: 遵守规则以维护秩序是很重要的。
words.en: To obey instructions, regulations, or guidelines; to act in accordance with established procedures.

words.ex: I forget where I put my keys.
words.ex_cn: 我忘记把钥匙放在哪儿了。
words.en: If you forget something, you fail to remember it.

words.tr: v. 忘记；遗忘；“forget”的过去式；
words.ex: I forgot my keys at home.
words.ex_cn: 我把钥匙忘在家里了。
words.en: If you forget something, you do not remember it.

words.tr: v. 忘记；“forget”的过去分词； adj. 被忘却的；
words.ex: The keys were forgotten on the table.
words.ex_cn: 钥匙被忘在桌子上。
words.en: If something is forgotten, it has been left behind or not remembered by someone.

words.ex: I remember my first day at school.
words.ex_cn: 我记得我上学的第一天。
words.en: If you remember people or events from the past, you still have an idea of them in your mind and you are able to think about them.

words.tr:
adj. 免费的；自由的；
adv. 免费地；自由地；
v. 释放；
words.ex: The museum offers free entry on Sundays.
words.ex_cn: 这个博物馆在周日免费入场。
words.en: If someone is free, they are able to do what they want to do, or go where they want to go, without being controlled or restricted.

words.ex: He wants freedom to speak his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他想要自由地表达自己的想法。
words.en: The condition of being free; the power to act or speak or think without externally imposed restraints.

words.ex: Children can play freely in the park.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们可以在公园里自由地玩耍。
words.en: If you can do something freely, you can do it without being controlled or restricted by anyone.

words.ex: You can download this app for free.
words.ex_cn: 你可以免费下载这个应用。
words.en: Without payment or charge; free of cost.

words.ex: He is my friend.
words.ex_cn: 他是我的朋友。
words.en: A friend is someone who you know well and like, but who is not related to you.

words.ex: He is a friendly boy who smiles at everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个友好的男孩，对每个人都微笑。
words.en: If someone is friendly, they behave in a pleasant, kind way, and like to be with other people.

words.ex: Their friendship lasted for twenty years.
words.ex_cn: 他们的友谊持续了二十年。
words.en: A friendship is a relationship between two or more friends.

words.tr:
adj. 一般的；普遍的；总的；大致的；首席的；
n. 将军；
words.ex: He gave a general answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个一般的回答。
words.en: A general is a high-ranking officer in the army or air force. In other contexts, general refers to something that is common, usual, or not specific.

words.ex: She generally wakes up at 7 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 她通常在早上七点起床。
words.en: In most cases; usually.

words.tr: phrase. 通常；大体上；一般而言
words.ex: In general, he likes to eat fruit.
words.ex_cn: 总的来说，他喜欢吃水果。
words.en: Usually; in most cases.

words.ex: She gave me a book.
words.ex_cn: 她给了我一本书。
words.en: To freely transfer the possession of something to someone; to cause or allow someone to have something.

words.tr: v. 给予；发出；“give”的过去式；
words.ex: She gave me a book.
words.ex_cn: 她给了我一本书。
words.en: Past tense of give, which means to freely transfer the possession of something to someone.

words.tr: v. 给予；“give”的过去分词； prep. 考虑到； adj. 规定的；
words.ex: She was given a gift by her friend.
words.ex_cn: 她的朋友给了她一份礼物。
words.en: If you say 'given' something, you mean taking that thing into account.

words.ex: He gave up smoking last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年戒烟了。
words.en: If you give up something, you stop doing it or having it.

words.tr: phrase. 分发；发出；发表；用尽
words.ex: He gives out books to the students.
words.ex_cn: 他把书分发给学生们。
words.en: To distribute or hand out something; to emit or produce something such as a sound or smell; to announce or make something known publicly.

words.ex: He goes to school every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天去上学。
words.en: To move or travel from one place to another.

words.ex: He went to the store yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 他昨天去商店了。
words.en: Went is the past tense of go.

words.tr: v. 去；走；“go”的过去分词； adj. 已往的；离去的；死去的；
words.ex: He is gone to the store.
words.ex_cn: 他去商店了。
words.en: No longer present; departed.

words.tr: 短语动词. 去散步；去走一走
words.ex: He goes for a walk after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚饭后去散步。
words.en: To go for a walk means to leave your home or workplace in order to walk somewhere, usually for pleasure or exercise.

words.tr: phrase. 仔细检查；复习；重做；转向；受欢迎
words.ex: I will go over my homework tonight.
words.ex_cn: 我今晚会复习我的家庭作业。
words.en: To examine or review something carefully; to cross over something.

words.ex: She is a good student.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个好学生。
words.en: Something that is good is of a high quality, standard, or level.

words.tr: adj. 更好的；更优秀的；“good”的比较级； adv. 更好地；“well”的比较级； v. 胜过；使更佳；
words.ex: This shirt is better than the other one.
words.ex_cn: 这件衬衫比那件更好。
words.en: If something is better, it is of a higher standard, quality, or level than something else, or than it was before.

words.tr:
adj. 最好的；
adv. 最好地；
n. 最佳物；佼佼者；最高水平；
words.ex: He is the best player on the team.
words.ex_cn: 他是队里最好的球员。
words.en: Of the most excellent, effective, or desirable type or quality.

words.tr:
adv. 好；对；满意地；
int. （用于表示惊讶，疑虑，接受等）好；
n. 井；
adj. 健康的；
words.ex: She sings well.
words.ex_cn: 她唱得很好。
words.en: In a good or satisfactory manner; in a thorough manner; in a manner that is appropriate or suitable.

words.tr: v. 生长；成长；渐渐变成；种植；
words.ex: The plant grows quickly in spring.
words.ex_cn: 这株植物在春天长得很快。
words.en: If someone or something grows, they increase in size, amount, or degree, often over a period of time.

words.tr: v. 成长；种植；养成；变得；“grow”的过去式；
words.ex: The tree grew tall near the house.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树在房子附近长高了。
words.en: Grew is the past tense of grow, which means to increase in size or amount, or to become something different.

words.tr: v. 种植；成长；渐渐变成；生长；“grow”的过去分词； adj. 成熟的；成年的；长大的；
words.ex: He grown tomatoes in his garden.
words.ex_cn: 他在花园里种植番茄。
words.en: Having reached maturity or full development; adult.

words.ex: The growth of the plant is slow in winter.
words.ex_cn: 这植物在冬天生长缓慢。
words.en: The process of increasing in physical size, number, value, or strength.

words.ex: He wants to grow up and be a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他想长大后当一名医生。
words.en: To grow up means to gradually change from being a child to being an adult. This process involves physical, emotional, and intellectual development.

words.tr:
n. 导游；指南；向导；
v. 指导；指引；
words.ex: The guide showed us the ancient temple.
words.ex_cn: 导游带我们参观了这座古庙。
words.en: A guide is someone who shows other people the way to a place in a difficult or unknown region. A guide is also a book that gives you information or instructions to help you do or understand something.

words.ex: The child is happy when he plays with his toys.
words.ex_cn: 当孩子玩玩具时，他很快乐。
words.en: If you are happy, you are feeling or showing pleasure or contentment.

words.ex: Children find happiness in simple games.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在简单的游戏中找到幸福。
words.en: Happiness is a state of well-being and contentment.

words.tr: adv. 快乐地；幸福地；幸运地；
words.ex: She smiled happily when she got the gift.
words.ex_cn: 她收到礼物时快乐地笑了。
words.en: In a happy manner; with happiness.

words.ex: He felt sad when his dog ran away.
words.ex_cn: 当他的狗跑掉时，他感到伤心。
words.en: Feeling or showing sorrow; unhappy.

words.tr: adj. 不快乐的；不高兴的；
words.ex: He looked unhappy after losing the game.
words.ex_cn: 他输掉比赛后看起来不快乐。
words.en: If you are unhappy, you are sad and depressed.

words.tr:
adj. 困难的；坚硬的；费劲的；
adv. 努力地；
words.ex: This math problem is hard.
words.ex_cn: 这个数学题很难。
words.en: If something is hard, it is very difficult to do or deal with. It can also mean that something is solid and firm, not soft or liquid.

words.tr: phrase. 努力工作；勤奋劳动
words.ex: He work hard every day to save money.
words.ex_cn: 他每天努力工作来攒钱。
words.en: To put a lot of effort into one's job or a task.

words.tr:
n. 伤害；损害；
v. 伤害；损害；
words.ex: The storm caused great harm to the crops.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴对庄稼造成了很大伤害。
words.en: To harm someone or something means to cause them physical injury or to damage them in some other way.

words.ex: Smoking is harmful to your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的健康有害。
words.en: Something that is harmful has a bad effect on something else, especially on a person's health.

words.ex: Smoking can do harm to your lungs.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟会对你的肺造成伤害。
words.en: To cause damage or injury to someone or something.

words.tr: phrase. 对…有害的；对…造成伤害的
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的肺有害。
words.en: To cause damage or injury to someone or something.

words.tr:
v. 帮助；
n. 帮助；
words.ex: He helps his sister with her homework.
words.ex_cn: 他帮助妹妹做作业。
words.en: If you help someone, you make it easier for them to do something, for example by doing part of the work for them or by giving them advice or information.

words.ex: This book is helpful for learning English.
words.ex_cn: 这本书对学习英语有帮助。
words.en: If you describe someone as helpful, you mean that they help you in some way, such as doing part of your job for you or by giving you advice or information.

words.ex: The child felt helpless when he lost his mother.
words.ex_cn: 当孩子失去妈妈时，他感到无助。
words.en: Unable to defend oneself or to act without help.
To assist or support someone.

words.uk: help ɛs biː wɪθ ɛs ðiː
words.us: help ɛs biː wɪθ ɛs ðiː
words.en: To assist someone with a particular task or problem.

words.tr:
v. 希望；
n. 希望；
words.ex: I hope it rains tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我希望明天下雨。
words.en: If you hope that something is true, or if you hope for something, you want it to be true or to happen, and you usually believe that it is possible or likely.

words.ex: He is hopeful about passing the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己通过考试抱有希望。
words.en: If you are hopeful, you are fairly confident that something that you want to happen will happen.

words.ex: He felt hopeless after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后感到毫无希望。
words.en: If you feel hopeless, you feel very unhappy because there seems to be no possibility of a better situation or success.

words.ex: I hope to see you soon.
words.ex_cn: 我希望很快见到你。
words.en: To desire or wish to perform a specific action.

words.ex: The soup is hot.
words.ex_cn: 汤是热的。
words.en: Having a high degree of heat or a high temperature.

words.tr: adj. 热的；热烈的；热的( hot的比较级 )；
words.ex: This summer is hotter than last year.
words.ex_cn: 今年夏天比去年更热。
words.en: Comparative form of 'hot', meaning having a high degree of heat or a high temperature.

words.ex: This summer is the hottest on record.
words.ex_cn: 今年夏天是有记录以来最热的。
words.en: Superlative form of 'hot', meaning having the highest temperature or being the most intense or popular.

words.tr:
n. 热度；热；
v. 加热；
words.ex: The heat of the sun made the road hot.
words.ex_cn: 太阳的热度让路面变得很热。
words.en: Heat is a form of energy that is transferred by a difference in temperature. It can also refer to the level of excitement or intensity in a situation.

words.tr:
n. 匆忙；
v. 赶快；
words.ex: He left in a hurry without saying goodbye.
words.ex_cn: 他匆忙离开，连再见都没说。
words.en: If you hurry somewhere, you go there quickly. If you hurry to do something, you start doing it quickly or do it more quickly than usual.

words.ex: He hurried to finish his homework before dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他匆忙做完作业，以便在晚饭前完成。

words.ex: He hurt his leg while playing soccer.
words.ex_cn: 他在踢足球时伤了腿。
words.en: If you hurt someone, you cause them to feel pain. If you hurt a part of your body, you feel pain there. If someone is hurt, they are injured.

words.ex: Can you imagine a world without phones?
words.ex_cn: 你能想象一个没有电话的世界吗？
words.en: To imagine means to form a mental image or concept of something that is not present or real.

words.ex: Children have a strong imagination.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们有很强的想象力。
words.en: The ability to form pictures or ideas in your mind of things that are new and exciting, or not real.

words.ex: Can you imagine doing homework every night?
words.ex_cn: 你能想象每天晚上都做作业吗？

words.ex: It is important to eat healthy food.
words.ex_cn: 吃健康的食物很重要。
words.en: Something that is important is very significant, is highly valued, or is necessary.

words.ex: The importance of homework is clear.
words.ex_cn: 作业的重要性是显而易见的。
words.en: The quality or state of being important; significance.

words.ex: Importantly, he finished his homework on time.
words.ex_cn: 重要的是，他按时完成了作业。
words.en: used to emphasize that something is important

words.ex: The small mistake was unimportant.
words.ex_cn: 这个小错误不重要。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as unimportant, you mean that they do not have much influence, effect, or value, and are therefore not worth serious consideration.

words.ex: He works hard to improve his English.
words.ex_cn: 他努力改善自己的英语。
words.en: To make something better, or to become better.

words.ex: There was a big improvement in his English skills.
words.ex_cn: 他的英语水平有了很大改进。
words.en: The act of making something better or the state of being made better; an example or instance of this.

words.ex: I want to improve English by reading books.
words.ex_cn: 我想通过读书来提高英语水平。

words.ex: The package includes a free book.
words.ex_cn: 这个套餐包括一本免费的书。
words.en: If one thing includes another, it has the other thing as one of its parts.

words.tr: prep. 包括；包含； v. 包括；包含；“include”的现在分词；
words.ex: The package includes apples, bananas, and oranges.
words.ex_cn: 这个包裹包括苹果、香蕉和橙子。
words.en: You use including to introduce examples of people or things that are part of the group of people or things that you are talking about.

words.tr:
v. 增加；增多；
n. 增加；增长；
words.ex: The company increased its profits last year.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司去年增加了利润。
words.en: To increase something means to make it larger in size, amount, or degree.

words.ex: The price will increase to $10.
words.ex_cn: 价格将涨到10美元。
words.en: To become or make something greater in amount, number, value, etc.

words.tr:
n. 影响（力）；
v. 影响；
words.ex: The teacher had a big influence on her students.
words.ex_cn: 老师对学生们有很大的影响。
words.en: The power to affect, control, or manipulate someone or something.

words.ex: Parents can have an influence on their children's habits.
words.ex_cn: 父母可以影响孩子的习惯。
words.en: To affect or change how someone or something develops, behaves, or thinks.

words.ex: Please inform me when the meeting starts.
words.ex_cn: 请在会议开始时通知我。
words.en: To inform someone means to tell them about something.

words.ex: The teacher gave us important information about the test.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了我们关于考试的重要信息。
words.en: Information is facts or details about a subject, event, or situation.

words.ex: He injured his leg while playing soccer.
words.ex_cn: 他在踢足球时伤了腿。
words.en: To injure someone means to cause them physical harm, for example in an accident or an attack.

words.tr: adj. 受伤的；受损害的； v. “injure”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The injured player was taken to the hospital.
words.ex_cn: 受伤的球员被送往医院。
words.en: If you are injured, you have been hurt, usually in an accident or attack.

words.ex: He got an injury while playing soccer.
words.ex_cn: 他在踢足球时受了伤。
words.en: An injury is damage to your body. It is a general term that refers to harm caused by accidents, falls, hits, weapons, etc.

words.ex: He invented a new machine to clean the house.
words.ex_cn: 他发明了一台新机器来打扫房子。
words.en: To invent something means to design or create it, especially something that has never been made before.

words.ex: The telephone was a great invention.
words.ex_cn: 电话是一项伟大的发明。
words.en: An invention is a unique or novel device, method, composition or process. It may be an improvement upon a machine or product, or a new process for creating an object or a result. An invention that achieves a completely unique function or result may be a radical breakthrough. Such works are novel and not obvious to others skilled in the same field.

words.tr: n. 发明家；发明者；创造者；
words.ex: Thomas Edison was a famous inventor.
words.ex_cn: 托马斯·爱迪生是一位著名的发明家。
words.en: An inventor is a person who has invented something, or whose job is to invent things.

words.ex: She invited her friend to dinner.
words.ex_cn: 她邀请她的朋友吃晚饭。
words.en: To invite someone means to ask them to come to a social event or to spend time with you socially.

words.ex: He received an invitation to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他收到了参加派对的邀请。
words.en: An invitation is a written or spoken request to come to an event such as a party, a meal, or a meeting.

words.ex: He wants to join the football team.
words.ex_cn: 他想加入足球队。
words.en: To become a member of a group or organization; to connect or fasten things together.

words.ex: She wants to join in the activity.
words.ex_cn: 她想参加这个活动。

words.tr:
n. 笑话；玩笑；
v. 开玩笑；
words.ex: He told a funny joke at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在派对上讲了一个有趣的笑话。
words.en: A joke is something that is said or done to make people laugh, especially a funny story or a trick played on someone.

words.ex: He tells a joke to make his friends laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他讲一个笑话来让朋友们笑。
words.en: Share a humorous story or remark to amuse others.

words.tr: phrase. 开玩笑；说笑话；逗乐
words.ex: He likes to make a joke when people are sad.
words.ex_cn: 当人们难过时，他喜欢讲个笑话。
words.en: To tell a funny story or make a humorous remark.

words.tr:
n. 法官；裁判；
v. 判断；评判；
words.ex: The judge announced the verdict in court.
words.ex_cn: 法官在法庭上宣布了判决。
words.en: A judge is a person who has the authority to decide questions brought before a court of law. To judge means to form an opinion or conclusion about something.

words.ex: She keeps the room clean every day.
words.ex_cn: 她每天保持房间干净。
words.en: To continue to have or hold something; to maintain a condition or position.

words.tr: v. 保持；保管；“keep”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: She kept the room clean every day.
words.ex_cn: 她每天保持房间干净。
words.en: Kept is the past tense and past participle of keep. To keep something means to have it or continue to have it in your possession, or to store it somewhere because you might need it later.

words.tr: phrase. 继续做某事；持续不断地做某事
words.ex: He keeps asking the same question.
words.ex_cn: 他不停地问同一个问题。
words.en: To continue performing a particular action or activity.

words.tr: phrase. 保守秘密；守口如瓶
words.ex: He can keep a secret very well.
words.ex_cn: 他很能保守秘密。
words.en: To keep a secret means to not tell anyone else about it.

words.ex: The lion killed a deer in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 狮子在森林里杀死了一只鹿。
words.en: To kill someone or something means to cause their death.

words.tr: v. 杀死；“kill”的现在分词； n. 杀人； adj. 致命的；
words.ex: The lion was killing a deer.
words.ex_cn: 那只狮子正在杀死一只鹿。
words.en: The act of causing death, especially deliberately; or something that causes death or is very difficult to endure.

words.tr: phrase. 消磨时间；打发时间
words.ex: He reads comics to kill time.
words.ex_cn: 他看漫画来打发时间。
words.en: To spend time doing something that is not particularly useful or interesting, especially while waiting for something else to happen.

words.ex: I know the answer.
words.ex_cn: 我知道答案。
words.en: To have information in your mind as a result of experience or because you have learned or been told it.

words.tr: v. 知道；认识；“know”的过去式；
words.ex: I knew the answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 我知道这个问题的答案。
words.en: To have information in your mind as a result of experience or because you have learned or been told it.

words.tr: adj. 已知的；知名的；出了名的； v. 知道；认识；“know”的过去分词；
words.ex: This is a known fact.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个已知的事实。
words.en: Recognized, familiar, or within the scope of knowledge.

words.tr: n. 知识；了解；学问；学识；
words.ex: He gained knowledge from reading books.
words.ex_cn: 他通过读书获得了知识。
words.en: Knowledge is information and understanding about a subject which a person has, or which all people have.

words.ex: He is knowledgeable about history and science.
words.ex_cn: 他对历史和科学都很博学。
words.en: Someone who is knowledgeable has or shows a clear understanding of many different facts about the world or about a particular subject.

words.w: it is known to all that
words.tr: phrase. 众所周知；大家都知道
words.ex: It is known to all that the sun rises in the east.
words.ex_cn: 众所周知，太阳从东方升起。

words.tr:
v. 笑；发笑；
n. 笑；笑声；
words.ex: He laugh when he saw the funny cat.
words.ex_cn: 他看到那只滑稽的猫时笑了。
words.en: To laugh means to make the spontaneous sounds and movements of the face and body that are the instinctive expressions of lively amusement and sometimes also of derision.

words.ex: The children's laughter filled the room.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们的笑声充满了房间。
words.en: The sound of people laughing, especially when it is loud and continuous.

words.ex: They laugh at his funny hat.
words.ex_cn: 他们因他的滑稽帽子而发笑。
words.en: To laugh at someone or something means to mock or ridicule them, often in a way that is not kind.

words.ex: I learn English every day.
words.ex_cn: 我每天学习英语。
words.en: To gain knowledge or skill by studying, practicing, being taught, or experiencing something.

words.tr: v. 学习；“learn”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 有学问的；
words.ex: He learned to read when he was five.
words.ex_cn: 他五岁时学会了阅读。
words.en: A learned person has gained a lot of knowledge by studying.

words.tr: v. 学习；“learn”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He learnt to read when he was five.
words.ex_cn: 他五岁时学会了阅读。
words.en: To gain knowledge or skill by studying, practicing, being taught, or experiencing something.

words.tr: n. 学习；学问； v. 学习；“learn”的现在分词；
words.ex: Learning takes time and practice.
words.ex_cn: 学习需要时间和练习。
words.en: The acquisition of knowledge or skills through study, experience, or being taught.

words.tr:
v. 离开；离去；留下；
n. 休假；
words.ex: He will leave the room after class.
words.ex_cn: 他下课后会离开房间。
words.en: To go away from a place or a person.

words.tr: v. 离开；“leave”的过去式和过去分词； n. 左；左边； adj. 左边的； adv. 向左；在左边；
words.ex: He left the house early this morning.
words.ex_cn: 他今天早上早早离开了家。
words.en: If there is a certain amount of something left, or if you have a certain amount of it left, it remains when the rest has gone or been used.

words.ex: We leave for sp on Monday.
words.ex_cn: 我们周一动身去某地。

words.ex: Let me help you with your homework.
words.ex_cn: 让我帮你做作业。
words.en: To allow or permit something to happen or someone to do something.

words.tr:
v. 躺；撒谎；
n. 谎言；
words.ex: The cat lies on the sofa.
words.ex_cn: 猫躺在沙发上。
words.en: If someone is lying, they are saying something which they know is not true.

words.tr: v. 放置；安放；下蛋；“lie”的过去式； adj. 外行的；非专业的；
words.ex: He lay the book on the table.
words.ex_cn: 他把书放在桌子上。
words.en: To put something down gently or carefully.

words.ex: The book has lain on the table for days.
words.ex_cn: 这本书已经放在桌子上好几天了。
words.en: Past participle of lie, meaning to be in or assume a horizontal or resting position on a supporting surface.

words.tr: v. 撒谎；“lie”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He lied about his age.
words.ex_cn: 他撒谎说了自己的年龄。
words.en: If someone lies, they say something that they know is not true.

words.ex: He runs like a cheetah.
words.ex_cn: 他跑得像猎豹一样。
words.en: To find something enjoyable or agreeable; to have a positive feeling towards someone or something.

words.tr: n. 嗜好；爱好； v. “like”的现在分词；
words.ex: His liking for chocolate is very strong.
words.ex_cn: 他对巧克力的嗜好非常强烈。
words.en: If you have a liking for something, you enjoy it or approve of it.

words.ex: He listens to music every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天听音乐。
words.en: If you listen to someone or something, you give your attention to a sound or to what someone says.

words.ex: He listens to music every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天听音乐。
words.en: To pay attention to someone or something in order to hear what is being said, sung, played, etc.

words.ex: Listen carefully to the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 仔细听老师讲。
words.en: Listen carefully: Pay close attention to what is being said without interrupting or being distracted.

words.tr:
v. 生活；居住；活着；
adj. 活的；现场的；实况转播的；
words.ex: They live in a small house near the park.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在公园附近的一所小房子里。
words.en: To live means to be alive, to have your home in a particular place, or to spend your life in a particular way.

words.ex: The fish is still alive in the water.
words.ex_cn: 这条鱼还在水里活着。
words.en: If people or animals are alive, they are not dead.

words.tr: adj. 充满生机的；活泼的；
words.ex: The market is lively with people and music.
words.ex_cn: 市场里人来人往，音乐欢快，充满生机。
words.en: If you describe someone as lively, you mean they are full of life, energy, or enthusiasm.

words.ex: She enjoys simple life in the countryside.
words.ex_cn: 她喜欢乡村里的简单生活。
words.en: Life is the existence of an individual human being or animal.

words.ex: The company decided to do a live broadcast of the event.
words.ex_cn: 公司决定对活动进行直播。
words.en: A live broadcast is a transmission of an event over television, radio, or the internet as it happens, without any delay.

words.tr:
v. 看；看上去；
n. 看；
words.ex: He looks at the sky.
words.ex_cn: 他看着天空。
words.en: To direct your eyes in a particular direction.

words.ex: She looks after her little brother every day.
words.ex_cn: 她每天照顾她的弟弟。
words.en: To take care of someone or something.

words.ex: He looks for his keys every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都找他的钥匙。
words.en: To search for something or someone.

words.ex: He looked through the book quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他快速翻阅了那本书。
words.en: To look through something means to examine or read it quickly or casually.

words.ex: He lost his keys yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 他昨天丢了钥匙。
words.en: If you lose something, you no longer have it or you cannot find it.

words.tr: adj. 丢失的； v. 丢失；输；“lose”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The lost keys were found under the table.
words.ex_cn: 丢失的钥匙在桌子下面找到了。
words.en: If you are lost, you do not know where you are or you are unable to find your way.

words.ex: The company suffered a big loss last year.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司去年遭受了巨大损失。
words.en: Loss is the fact of no longer having something or having less of it than you used to have, or the process by which this happens.

words.tr: phrase. v. 走开，消失；迷路
words.ex: He told the noisy boy to get lost.
words.ex_cn: 他让那个吵闹的男孩走开。
words.en: If you tell someone to get lost, you are telling them in a rude way to go away.

words.tr:
v. 热爱；爱；
n. 爱；爱情；爱好的事物；
words.ex: I love playing football with my friends.
words.ex_cn: 我热爱和朋友们一起踢足球。
words.en: Love is a very strong feeling of affection towards someone that you are romantically or sexually attracted to.

words.ex: The little girl has a lovely smile.
words.ex_cn: 这个小女孩有一个可爱的笑容。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as lovely, you mean that they are very beautiful and therefore pleasing to look at or be with.

words.tr: adj. 钟爱…的；爱好…的； v. “love”的现在分词；
words.ex: She is a loving mother who always cares for her children.
words.ex_cn: 她是一位钟爱孩子的母亲，总是关心她的孩子们。
words.en: Showing or feeling love; affectionate.

words.ex: The rain made the road wet.
words.ex_cn: 雨使得道路变湿了。
words.en: To create, produce, or prepare something, especially by putting parts together or by combining materials.

words.tr: v. 制作；使得；做；“make”的过去式和过去分词； adj. …制作的；
words.ex: She made a cake for her brother.
words.ex_cn: 她为弟弟做了一个蛋糕。
words.en: To produce something, often using a particular material or method.

words.uk: meɪk ɛs biː dʌʊ ɛs ɛθ
words.us: meɪk ɛs biː dʌʊ ɛs ɛθ

words.tr: phrase. 编造；组成；弥补；化妆；和好
words.ex: He made up a story to explain his delay.
words.ex_cn: 他编了一个故事来解释他的迟到。
words.en: To make up means to form something by combining or assembling parts, to invent a story or excuse, to apply cosmetics, or to reconcile after a disagreement.

words.tr: 由……制成（表示材料，强调原材料未发生根本性变化）
words.ex: The table is made of wood.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子是木头做的。
words.en: If something is made of a particular material, that material was used to build it.

words.ex: Paper is made from wood.
words.ex_cn: 纸是由木头制成的。
words.en: To be produced or created from a particular material or substance.

words.ex: I managed to finish my homework before dinner.
words.ex_cn: 我设法在晚饭前完成了作业。
words.en: To manage means to be in charge of or control something, especially a business or a group of people.

words.ex: Good management helps a company grow.
words.ex_cn: 良好的管理有助于公司发展。
words.en: The control and organization of something, especially a business and its employees.

words.tr: phrase. 设法做成某事；成功完成某事
words.ex: He managed to finish his homework before dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他设法在晚饭前完成了作业。
words.en: Succeed in doing something, often despite difficulties.

words.tr:
v. 意思；导致；打算；
n. 平均数；
adj. 低劣；平均；
words.ex: What does this word mean?
words.ex_cn: 这个词是什么意思？
words.en: If you want to know what a word, a sentence, or an expression means, you want to know what it refers to or what its significance is.

words.tr: v. 意味着；打算；表示…的意思；“mean”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He meant to help, but he made it worse.
words.ex_cn: 他本意是想帮忙，但却让情况更糟了。
words.en: If you mean to do something, you intend or plan to do it.

words.tr: n. 意思；意义； v. 表示…的意思；意思；“mean”的现在分词；
words.ex: What is the meaning of this word?
words.ex_cn: 这个词的意思是什么？
words.en: The meaning of something is what it expresses or represents.

words.ex: He gave a meaningful speech that helped many people.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一次有意义的演讲，帮助了很多人。
words.en: If you describe something as meaningful, you mean that it is important, serious, or useful in some way.

words.ex: The talk was meaningless and boring.
words.ex_cn: 这场谈话毫无意义且无聊。
words.en: If something is meaningless, it has no meaning, or seems to have no meaning.

words.ex: He means quitting his job to travel.
words.ex_cn: 他意思是辞掉工作去旅行。
words.en: To involve or signify doing something.

words.tr: phrase. 打算做某事；有意做某事
words.ex: He means to finish his homework before dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他打算在晚饭前完成作业。
words.en: To intend or plan to do something, often with a specific purpose.

words.ex: We will meet at the park tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我们明天将在公园见面。
words.en: To come into the presence of someone by chance or arrangement.

words.tr: v. 遇见；见面；满足；“meet”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: I met my friend at the park.
words.ex_cn: 我在公园里遇见了我的朋友。
words.en: Met is the past tense and past participle of meet. To meet someone means to come into their presence by chance or arrangement.

words.tr: n. 会议；会面； v. 遇见；见面；“meet”的现在分词；
words.ex: The meeting starts at 9 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 会议上午九点开始。
words.en: A meeting is an event in which a group of people come together to discuss things or make decisions.

words.tr:
v. 移动；搬家；
n. 行动；移动；
words.ex: Please move the chair.
words.ex_cn: 请移动椅子。
words.en: To change position or to cause something or someone to change position, especially in a particular direction or to a particular place.

words.tr: n. 运动；动作；活动；乐章；
words.ex: The movement of the sun changes the shadow.
words.ex_cn: 太阳的运动改变了影子。
words.en: The act or process of moving or being moved; a change of position or place.

words.tr: v. 移动；搬家；搬动；行动；进展； adj. 受感动的；受感动的 v. 移动，搬动( move的过去式和过去分词 )；
words.ex: He moved the chair to the window.
words.ex_cn: 他把椅子移到了窗边。
words.en: If you are moved by something, it makes you feel strongly emotional, often causing you to want to help or show sympathy. As a verb, it refers to the action of changing position or causing something to change position.

words.tr: v. 移动；“move”的现在分词；搬家； adj. 运动的；感人的；动人的；可移动的；
words.ex: The boy is moving his toy car.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩正在移动他的玩具车。
words.en: If something is moving, it makes you feel strongly touched or emotional.

words.tr:
adv. 非常地；
adj. 多；许多；
pron. 许多；
words.ex: She is much happier now.
words.ex_cn: 她现在快乐多了。
words.en: A large amount or to a great degree.

words.tr:
adv. 更加；
adj. 更多的；
pron. 更多的人或物；
words.ex: She wants to learn more about science.
words.ex_cn: 她想更深入了解科学。
words.en: You use 'more' to indicate that there is a greater amount of something than before or than average, or than something else. You can use 'more' with a noun to indicate that there is a greater amount of it than before or than average, or than something else.

words.tr:
adv. 最；
pron. 大部分；
adj. 最多的；大多数的；
words.ex: He is most tired after work.
words.ex_cn: 他下班后最累。
words.en: You use most to refer to the majority of a group of things or people or the largest part of something.

words.ex: He ate too much candy and felt sick.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了太多糖果，感觉不舒服。
words.en: An excessive amount; more than is necessary or desirable.

words.ex: He loves listening to music every night.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢每天晚上听音乐。
words.en: Music is the pattern of sounds produced by people singing or playing instruments.

words.ex: He is a musician who plays the guitar.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位弹吉他的音乐家。
words.en: A musician is a person who plays a musical instrument, especially as a profession, or is musically talented.

words.tr:
adj. 音乐的；擅长音乐的；
n. 音乐剧；音乐歌舞片；
words.ex: He loves musical songs.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢音乐的歌曲。
words.en: Relating to music; having the pleasant sound of music.

words.ex: His nature is kind and patient.
words.ex_cn: 他的本性是善良且有耐心的。
words.en: Nature refers to the physical world and everything in it that is not made by people, including plants, animals, mountains, oceans, stars, etc. It can also refer to the basic or inherent features, character, or qualities of something.

words.ex: The children played in the natural park.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在自然公园里玩耍。
words.en: Existing in or caused by nature; not made or caused by humankind.

words.tr: adv. 自然地；理所当然地；
words.ex: Babies cry naturally when they are hungry.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿饿了时会自然地哭。
words.en: in a natural manner; as a matter of course; by nature

words.tr: phrase. 就其本质而言；天生地
words.ex: He is by nature a quiet person.
words.ex_cn: 他天性安静。
words.en: If someone has a particular quality by nature, they have it as a natural part of their character.

words.tr:
prep. 靠近；在…附近；
adj. 近的；
adv. 近地；
words.ex: The cat is near the window.
words.ex_cn: 猫靠近窗户。
words.en: If something is near, it is not far away in distance or time.

words.tr: adj. 近的；近似；近的( near的比较级 )；
words.ex: The park is nearer than the school.
words.ex_cn: 公园比学校更近。
words.en: At a shorter distance in space or time; closer.

words.tr:
adj. 近的；（亲属关系）；
adv. 最近的；
words.ex: The nearest store is just around the corner.
words.ex_cn: 最近的商店就在拐角处。
words.en: The superlative form of 'near', meaning closest in distance or relationship.

words.tr:
adj. 附近的；
adv. 在附近；
words.ex: There is a park nearby my house.
words.ex_cn: 我家附近有一个公园。
words.en: If something is nearby, it is only a short distance away.

words.tr:
v. 需要；
n. 需要；
words.ex: I need help with my homework.
words.ex_cn: 我需要帮助做作业。
words.en: If you need something, you must have it because it is essential.

words.tr: v. 需要；“need”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He needed help with his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他需要帮助做作业。
words.en: required because it is essential or very important

words.tr: phrase. 需要做某事；必须去做某事
words.ex: I need to do my homework now.
words.ex_cn: 我现在需要做我的家庭作业。
words.en: To have to do something because it is necessary or important.

words.ex: He bought a new bike yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 他昨天买了一辆新自行车。
words.en: Recently made, invented, introduced, or discovered; not existing before.

words.ex: The newness of the phone excited her.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机的新颖让她兴奋。
words.en: The quality of being new; novelty.

words.ex: He was newly hired as a teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他最近被聘为老师。
words.en: Newly means something that has happened or been done recently.

words.ex: The old man walks slowly in the park.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人在公园里慢慢走路。
words.en: Having lived or existed for a long time; no longer young or new.

words.ex: The noise from the street kept me awake.
words.ex_cn: 街道上的噪声让我睡不着。
words.en: Noise is a sound, especially one that is loud, unpleasant, or disturbing.

words.ex: The children are noisy in the classroom.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在教室里很吵。
words.en: A noisy place is full of a lot of loud or unpleasant sounds.

words.ex: The children are playing noisily in the yard.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在院子里吵闹地玩耍。
words.en: In a manner that makes a lot of noise; loudly and disruptively.

words.ex: The scientist observe the birds every morning.
words.ex_cn: 科学家每天早上观察鸟类。
words.en: If you observe a person or thing, you watch them carefully, especially in order to learn something about them.

words.tr: n. 观察；观测；注意；监视；(观察后的）意见；
words.ex: The scientist made an observation about the bird's behavior.
words.ex_cn: 科学家对这只鸟的行为进行了观察。
words.en: The act of noticing or watching something carefully in order to gain information.

words.tr:
v. 提供；
n. 提供；提议；报价；
words.ex: He offers help to his classmates.
words.ex_cn: 他向同学提供帮助。
