words.ex: He gets dressed at seven o'clock every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上七点穿衣服。
words.en: To put on clothes.

words.tr:
n. 饮料；酒；
v. 喝；喝酒；
words.ex: I bought a cold drink at the store.
words.ex_cn: 我在商店买了一瓶冷饮。
words.en: To take liquid into the mouth and swallow it; a liquid that can be swallowed as refreshment or nourishment.

words.ex: He drank water after running.
words.ex_cn: 他跑步后喝了水。
words.en: The past tense of 'drink', meaning to take liquid into the mouth and swallow it.

words.tr: v. 喝；喝酒；“drink”的过去分词； adj. 喝醉的；
words.ex: He has drunk all the water.
words.ex_cn: 他喝了所有的水。
words.en: If someone is drunk, they have consumed so much alcohol that it has affected their ability to think and speak clearly.

words.ex: He works hard to earn money.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以赚取收入。
words.en: To earn means to gain something, especially money or respect, through your own efforts or work.

words.tr: n. 所赚的钱； v. 获得；赚得；“earn”的现在分词；
words.ex: His earning from the job is enough to pay rent.
words.ex_cn: 他工作的收入足以支付房租。
words.en: Money that is earned by working.

words.ex: He works at a store to earn money.
words.ex_cn: 他在商店工作赚钱。
words.en: To receive money as payment for work or services performed.

words.tr: n. 影响；作用；效果；效应；
words.ex: The new law had a big effect on traffic.
words.ex_cn: 新法律对交通产生了很大影响。
words.en: A change that is a result or consequence of an action or other cause.

words.ex: This medicine is effective against colds.
words.ex_cn: 这种药对感冒有效。
words.en: Something that is effective works well and produces the results that were intended.

words.ex: Smoking has an effect on your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对健康有影响。
words.en: To cause a change or influence something.

words.ex: He made a big effort to finish the project on time.
words.ex_cn: 他努力完成这个项目，按时交工。
words.en: If you make an effort to do something, you try hard to do it.

words.w: make an effort to do sth
words.tr: phrase. 努力做某事；尽力去做某事
words.ex: He makes an effort to go to school on time.
words.ex_cn: 他努力按时上学。
words.en: To try hard to do something, especially when it is difficult or requires a lot of work.

words.ex: The electric lamp lights up the room.
words.ex_cn: 电灯照亮了房间。
words.en: Something that is electric works by means of electricity, is powered by electricity, or produces electricity.

words.ex: The town lost electricity during the storm.
words.ex_cn: 风暴期间，这个城镇停电了。
words.en: A form of energy resulting from the existence of charged particles (such as electrons or protons), either statically as an accumulation of charge or dynamically as a current.

words.ex: He embarrassed himself in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他在全班同学面前让自己丢脸了。
words.en: If you embarrass someone, you make them feel shy, ashamed, or guilty about something.

words.tr: adj. 尴尬的；窘迫的； v. “embarrass”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He felt embarrassed when he tripped in front of everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他在大家面前绊倒时感到很尴尬。
words.en: If you are embarrassed, you feel shy or ashamed because of something that you have done or that has happened to you.

words.tr: adj. 令人尴尬的；令人为难的； v. “embarrass”的现在分词；
words.ex: It was embarrassing when I tripped in front of everyone.
words.ex_cn: 我在大家面前绊倒了，很尴尬。
words.en: Something that is embarrassing makes you feel shy or ashamed.

words.tr:
n. 结束；尽头；目标；末端；
v. 结束；终止；
words.ex: The end of the movie made everyone cry.
words.ex_cn: 电影的结尾让所有人都哭了。
words.en: The end of something such as a period of time, an event, a book, or a film is the last part of it or the point at which it stops.

words.ex: In the end, he chose to go home.
words.ex_cn: 最后，他选择回家。
words.en: finally, after everything has been considered or done

words.ex: He will call you at the end of the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他会在会议结束时给你打电话。
words.en: Indicates the final part of a period of time, an event, a process, or a physical object.

words.ex: China uses a lot of energy from coal.
words.ex_cn: 中国使用大量煤炭能源。
words.en: Energy is the ability and strength to do active physical things and the feeling that you are full of physical power and life.

words.tr: adj. 有活力的；精力旺盛的；
words.ex: The energetic boy ran around the park all afternoon.
words.ex_cn: 这个有活力的男孩整个下午都在公园里跑来跑去。
words.en: Someone who is energetic is very active and does not tire easily.

words.tr:
v. 逃避；逃走；
n. 逃脱；逃避；
words.ex: He tried to escape from the prison.
words.ex_cn: 他试图逃离监狱。
words.en: To escape means to get away from a place or a situation that you are in, especially because it is difficult or dangerous to stay there.

words.ex: The boy tried to escape from the burning house.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩试图从着火的房子里逃出来。
words.en: To get away from a place or a situation that is dangerous, unpleasant, or difficult.

words.ex: I like all fruits, especially apples.
words.ex_cn: 我喜欢所有的水果，尤其是苹果。
words.en: You use especially to emphasize that what you are saying applies more to one thing or situation than to others.

words.ex: This is an especial day for me.
words.ex_cn: 今天对我来说是个特别的日子。
words.en: Used to emphasize that something is more important or significant than other things of the same kind.

words.ex: He gave the exact time of the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他给出了会议的确切时间。
words.en: If you describe something as exact, you mean that it is precise and accurate in all its details.

words.tr: adv. 确切地；正是；准确地；
words.ex: He arrived exactly at 8 o'clock.
words.ex_cn: 他正好在八点到达。
words.en: In a precise manner; accurately.

words.ex: The police will examine the crime scene.
words.ex_cn: 警察将调查犯罪现场。
words.en: If you examine something, you look at it carefully.

words.ex: The doctor did an examination of his arm.
words.ex_cn: 医生对他手臂进行了检查。
words.en: An examination is a formal test that you take to show your knowledge or ability in a particular subject, or to obtain a qualification.

words.ex: He passed the exam with high marks.
words.ex_cn: 他以高分通过了考试。
words.en: An exam is a formal test that you take to show your knowledge or ability in a particular subject, or to obtain a qualification.

words.ex: This is a good example of teamwork.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个团队合作的好例子。
words.en: An example is a particular instance of something that is representative of a group or used to illustrate a point.

words.ex: He likes apples, for example.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢苹果，例如。
words.en: Used when you want to give a specific instance or illustration of what you are talking about.

words.ex: He likes fruits such as apples and bananas.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢苹果和香蕉这样的水果。
words.en: Used to introduce examples of something that has been mentioned.

words.tr:
prep. 除了；
conj. 只是；
words.ex: Everyone went to the party except Tom.
words.ex_cn: 除了汤姆，大家都去参加派对了。
words.en: You use except to introduce the only thing or person that a statement does not apply to, or a fact that prevents a statement from being completely true.

words.ex: Everyone came to the party except for Tom.
words.ex_cn: 除了汤姆，大家都来参加派对了。
words.en: You use except for to introduce the only thing or person that prevents a statement from being completely true.

words.ex: Please excuse me for being late.
words.ex_cn: 请原谅我迟到了。
words.en: To excuse someone means to forgive them for something they have done wrong or to allow them not to do something that they should do.

words.tr:
n. 锻炼；行使；练习；
v. 运用；使用；锻炼；
words.ex: He does exercise every morning to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上锻炼以保持健康。
words.en: Physical activity that you do to make your body strong and healthy.

words.ex: He takes exercise every morning in the park.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上在公园里锻炼。
words.en: To perform physical activities in order to stay healthy and improve physical fitness.

words.ex: He does exercise every morning to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上做运动来保持健康。
words.en: To perform physical activity to maintain or improve health and fitness.

words.ex: I expect a gift on my birthday.
words.ex_cn: 我期待在生日时收到一份礼物。
words.en: If you expect something, you believe that it is likely to happen or that it will be the case.

words.ex: His expectation was to pass the test.
words.ex_cn: 他的期待是通过考试。
words.en: An expectation is a belief about what might happen in the future, especially about something that you think is likely or that you hope will happen.

words.ex: I expect to finish the report by Friday.
words.ex_cn: 我期望在周五前完成报告。

words.ex: The phone is expensive.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机很贵。
words.en: Costing a lot of money; having a high price.

words.ex: This shirt is cheap and nice.
words.ex_cn: 这件衬衫又便宜又好看。
words.en: If something is cheap, it costs less money than usual or than you expected.

words.ex: This store sells inexpensive clothes.
words.ex_cn: 这家店卖不贵的衣服。
words.en: Something that is inexpensive does not cost a lot of money.

words.ex: Please explain clearly what you mean.
words.ex_cn: 请清楚地解释你的意思。

words.tr: phrase. 表达某人的感情；抒发某人的情感
words.ex: He can express his feelings through music.
words.ex_cn: 他可以通过音乐表达自己的感情。

words.ex: I am familiar with this song.
words.ex_cn: 我熟悉这首歌。
words.en: If someone or something is familiar to you, you recognize them or know them well.

words.ex: He is familiar with basic math.
words.ex_cn: 他熟悉基础数学。
words.en: If you are familiar with something, you know or understand it well.

words.tr:
n. 脂肪；
adj. 肥的；
words.ex: This food has too much fat.
words.ex_cn: 这种食物含有太多脂肪。
words.en: Fat is a substance contained in foods such as meat, cheese, and butter, which is used by the body to produce energy or stored in the body as a layer.

words.tr: adj. 更胖的；更肥胖的（fat 的比较级）
words.ex: The cat is getting fatter every day.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫每天都在变胖。
words.en: Comparative adjective meaning having more body fat.

words.tr:
n. 力量；力；兵力；武力；
v. 强迫；促使；推动；
words.ex: The force of the wind broke the tree.
words.ex_cn: 风的力量折断了那棵树。
words.en: Force is a physical power or strength possessed by a living being; it is also an influence that can change the motion of an object.

words.uk: fɔːs ɛs biː tuː dʊ ɛs ʌθ
words.us: fɔːrs ɛs biː tuː dʊ ɛs θ
words.en: To compel someone to undertake a specific action.

words.ex: I forgive you for being late.
words.ex_cn: 我原谅你迟到了。
words.en: If you forgive someone who has done something bad or wrong, you stop being angry with them and stop blaming them.

words.ex: She forgave him for being late.
words.ex_cn: 她原谅了他迟到。
words.en: to stop feeling angry or resentful toward someone for an offense, flaw, or mistake

words.ex: He was forgiven for lying.
words.ex_cn: 他因为撒谎而被原谅了。
words.en: If you forgive someone who has done something wrong, you stop being angry with them and stop blaming them.

words.tr:
v. （使）结冰；（使）冻结；
n. 严寒期；冻结；
words.ex: The water will freeze in cold weather.
words.ex_cn: 水在寒冷的天气里会结冰。
words.en: If a liquid or a substance containing a liquid freezes, or if something freezes it, it becomes solid because of low temperatures.

words.tr: v. 冻结；呆住；冻住；“freeze”的过去式；
words.ex: The lake froze in winter.
words.ex_cn: 冬天湖面结冰了。
words.en: If a liquid or a substance containing a liquid freezes, or if something freezes it, it becomes solid because of low temperatures.

words.tr: adj. 冰冻的；冻结的； v. “freeze”的过去分词；
words.ex: The frozen fish tastes fresh.
words.ex_cn: 冰冻的鱼尝起来很新鲜。
words.en: If something is frozen, it has been turned into ice or has become very hard because of cold temperature.

words.tr: adj. 新鲜的；新的；刚发生的；
words.ex: She bought fresh apples from the market.
words.ex_cn: 她从市场买了新鲜的苹果。
words.en: Fresh food has been picked or produced recently, and has not been preserved, for example by being frozen or put in a tin.

words.tr: phrase. 新鲜空气；清新的空气
words.ex: He likes to breathe fresh air in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在早上呼吸新鲜空气。
words.en: Fresh air refers to air that is clean and not polluted, often considered beneficial for health.

words.ex: The loud noise frightened the child.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音吓到了孩子。
words.en: If something or someone frightens you, they cause you to suddenly feel afraid, anxious, or nervous.

words.tr: adj. 惊吓的；受惊的；害怕的； v. “frighten”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The child was frightened by the loud noise.
words.ex_cn: 孩子被巨大的噪音吓到了。
words.en: If you are frightened, you are anxious or afraid, often because of something that has just happened or that you think may happen.

words.tr: adj. 引起恐惧的；使惊恐的；骇人的； v. “frighten”的现在分词；
words.ex: The dark forest looked frightening at night.
words.ex_cn: 那个黑暗的森林在晚上看起来很吓人。
words.en: If you say that something is frightening, you mean that it makes you feel afraid or anxious.

words.tr:
n. 前面；前线；
adj. 前面的；
words.ex: The front of the house has a big garden.
words.ex_cn: 房子的前面有一个大花园。
words.en: The front is the part of something that faces forward or is the most important or prominent part.

words.ex: The cat is sitting in front of the house.
words.ex_cn: 猫坐在房子前面。
words.en: If someone or something is in front of a particular thing, they are facing it, ahead of it, or close to the front part of it.

words.tr: phrase. 在……前部（指某物体内部的前端位置）
words.ex: The teacher stands in the front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 老师站在教室前面。
words.en: At the foremost part or position of something.

words.tr:
adj. 满的；充满的；
adv. 完全地；
words.ex: The glass is full of water.
words.ex_cn: 这个玻璃杯装满了水。
words.en: Containing or holding as much or as many as possible; having no empty space.

words.ex: The box is full of toys.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子里装满了玩具。
words.en: To contain or hold as much or as many as possible; to be filled with something.

words.tr:
n. 大学毕业生；
v. 毕业；
words.ex: He is a graduate of Harvard University.
words.ex_cn: 他是哈佛大学的毕业生。
words.en: A graduate is a person who has successfully completed a degree at a university or college and has received a certificate or diploma stating this. To graduate means to successfully complete a degree at a university or college.

words.ex: She combs her hair every morning.
words.ex_cn: 她每天早上梳头发。
words.en: Hair is the fine threadlike strands growing from the skin of humans and animals, or the mass of such strands growing from the skin of a person's head.

words.tr: 短语动词. 剪头发；理发
words.ex: He has his hair cut every month.
words.ex_cn: 他每个月都剪一次头发。
words.en: To get a haircut; to have someone cut one's hair.

words.tr:
n. 一半；
adj. 一半的；
adv. 一半地；
words.ex: He ate half of the apple.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了苹果的一半。
words.en: One of two equal parts into which something is or can be divided.

words.ex: Half of the students passed the exam.
words.ex_cn: 一半的学生通过了考试。
words.en: Half of is used to indicate that something is divided into two equal parts.

words.tr:
n. 手；
v. 交；递；给；
words.ex: He waved his hand to say hello.
words.ex_cn: 他挥挥手打招呼。
words.en: The part of the body at the end of the arm that is used for holding, moving, touching, and feeling things.

words.ex: He will hand in his homework tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天交作业。
words.en: To give something to someone in authority, especially a piece of work or a document.

words.ex: The teacher will hand out the papers now.
words.ex_cn: 老师现在会分发试卷。
words.en: To distribute something to a group of people.

words.tr:
v. 悬挂；吊；
n. 悬挂；
words.ex: He hangs a picture on the wall.
words.ex_cn: 他把一幅画挂在墙上。
words.en: To hang something means to attach it to something else so that it is supported from above and does not touch the ground.

words.tr: v. 悬挂；“hang”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He hung the picture on the wall.
words.ex_cn: 他把画挂在墙上。
words.en: to suspend or be suspended from above with the lower part dangling free

words.tr: v. 绞死；“hang”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He was found guilty and sentenced to be hanged.
words.ex_cn: 他被判有罪并被判处绞刑。
words.en: Put to death by hanging as a form of punishment.

words.ex: The accident happened yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 事故昨天发生了。
words.en: If something happens, it occurs as a result of a situation or course of action.

words.tr: 短语动词. 碰巧做某事
words.ex: I happened to see her at the bus stop.
words.ex_cn: 我碰巧在公交站看到了她。
words.en: To do something by chance or without planning.

words.ex: I hate waking up early.
words.ex_cn: 我讨厌早起。
words.en: To hate someone or something means to feel intense or passionate dislike for them.

words.ex: I hate doing homework on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 我讨厌在周末做作业。

words.tr: v. 讨厌去做某事；不愿意做某事
words.ex: I hate to wake up early on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 我讨厌在周末早起。
words.en: To feel strong aversion or reluctance to perform a specific action.

words.ex: Good food and sleep help maintain health.
words.ex_cn: 良好的饮食和睡眠有助于保持健康。
words.en: The condition of a person's body or mind, especially in terms of the presence or absence of illnesses, injuries, or impairments.

words.ex: She eats healthy food every day.
words.ex_cn: 她每天吃健康的食物。
words.en: Someone who is healthy is well and is not suffering from any illness.

words.tr: phrase. 保持健康；维持健康状态
words.ex: He eats vegetables and runs every day to keep healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他每天吃蔬菜并跑步以保持健康。
words.en: To maintain good physical condition and well-being.

words.ex: He runs every morning to keep fit.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上跑步以保持健康。
words.en: To maintain one's health and physical condition through regular exercise and a healthy diet.

words.ex: I hear birds singing in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 我听到早晨鸟儿在唱歌。
words.en: To perceive or become aware of (sound) through the ear.

words.tr: v. 听；听见；“hear”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: I heard a bird singing outside.
words.ex_cn: 我听到外面有一只鸟在唱歌。
words.en: To perceive or become aware of (sound) by the ear.

words.ex: I have never heard of that song before.
words.ex_cn: 我以前从未听说过那首歌。
words.en: To become aware of something through hearing about it from someone else.

words.ex: I just heard about the new park in town.
words.ex_cn: 我刚刚听说了镇上的新公园。
words.en: To become aware of something through being told about it.

words.ex: The box is heavy.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子很重。
words.en: Something that is heavy weighs a lot.

words.ex: It rained heavily last night.
words.ex_cn: 昨晚雨下得很大。
words.en: To a great degree; in large amounts.

words.tr: 短语动词，情不自禁地做某事；忍不住做某事
words.ex: I can't help laughing when I see that funny cat.
words.ex_cn: 当我看到那只搞笑的猫时，我忍不住笑。
words.en: To be unable to stop oneself from doing something, often because it is irresistible or habitual.

words.tr:
v. 隐藏；躲藏；
n. 兽皮；
words.ex: He hides the key under the mat.
words.ex_cn: 他把钥匙藏在垫子下面。
words.en: To conceal something or someone from view or discovery.

words.ex: He hid the key under the mat.
words.ex_cn: 他把钥匙藏在门垫下面。
words.en: to put or keep out of sight; to prevent from being seen or discovered.

words.tr: adj. 隐藏的； v. 隐藏；“hide”的过去分词；
words.ex: The keys are hidden under the mat.
words.ex_cn: 钥匙藏在垫子下面。
words.en: If something is hidden, it is not easily noticed or found.

words.tr:
v. 打；击；碰撞；袭击；抨击；达到；
n. 打；击；碰撞；袭击；(演出等)成功；
words.ex: He hit the ball with a bat.
words.ex_cn: 他用球棒打了球。
words.en: If you hit someone or something, you deliberately touch them with a lot of force, with your hand or an object held in your hand.

words.tr:
v. 抓住；持有；容纳；保留；举行；
n. 拿；控制；持；
words.ex: He held the rope tightly.
words.ex_cn: 他紧紧抓住了绳子。
words.en: To have or keep in the hand; to maintain in a grasp; to keep in a specified state, relation, or position; to contain or be capable of containing; to have in one's possession; to keep back from action; to delay the action or effect of; to keep in custody; to bear, sustain, or support; to have or maintain in the mind; to consider or esteem; to assert or affirm; to organize and carry on; to have the ownership or use of; to keep from falling or moving; to remain unbroken or unyielding; to remain attached or faithful; to remain valid or effective.

words.ex: They will hold a meeting tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他们明天将召开会议。
words.en: To organize and conduct a formal gathering of people for discussion or decision-making.

words.ex: We went to the beach during the holiday.
words.ex_cn: 我们在假日去了海滩。
words.en: A holiday is a day of festivity or recreation when no work is done.

words.ex: They are on holiday in Spain.
words.ex_cn: 他们正在西班牙度假。
words.en: If you are on holiday, you are spending a period of time away from work or school, usually in order to relax or travel.

words.ex: They take a holiday in summer.
words.ex_cn: 他们夏天放假。
words.en: To take time off from work or routine to relax or travel.

words.tr: adj. 诚实的；正直的；坦率的；
words.ex: He gave an honest answer to the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他向老师给出了一个诚实的回答。
words.en: If you describe someone as honest, you mean that they always tell the truth, and do not try to deceive people or break the law.

words.ex: I honestly don't know the answer.
words.ex_cn: 我诚实地不知道答案。
words.en: In a way that is truthful and sincere; without deceit.

words.ex: Honesty is important in friendship.
words.ex_cn: 诚实在友谊中很重要。
words.en: The quality of being honest, which involves being truthful, sincere, and free from deceit or fraud.

words.tr:
n. 主人；主持人；
v. 主持；
words.ex: The host welcomed us with tea and cookies.
words.ex_cn: 主人用茶和饼干欢迎了我们。
words.en: A host is a person who receives or entertains guests, especially in their own home. A host is also a person who presents a television or radio program.

words.tr: n. 女主人；女房东；女招待；女主持人；
words.ex: The hostess welcomed us with a smile.
words.ex_cn: 女主人微笑着欢迎我们。
words.en: A woman who receives or entertains guests in a social or official capacity; a woman who is in charge of a particular event or place and who welcomes and looks after the people who attend.

words.ex: The dog is huge.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗很大。
words.en: Extremely large in size or amount.

words.tr: adv. 非常地；极多地；巨大地；
words.ex: The movie was hugely popular.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影非常受欢迎。
words.en: To an extremely great extent or degree; immensely.

words.tr:
adj. 人的；人类的；
n. 人；人类；
words.ex: Human emotions are complex and powerful.
words.ex_cn: 人的情感复杂而强大。
words.en: A human is a member of the species Homo sapiens, distinguished from other animals by superior mental development, power of articulate speech, and upright stance.

words.ex: Every human being deserves respect.
words.ex_cn: 每一个人都应得到尊重。
words.en: A human being is a man, woman, or child.

words.ex: Humans need water to survive.
words.ex_cn: 人类需要水来生存。
words.en: Human beings collectively; the human race.

words.tr: adj. 生病的；坏的；不舒服的；
words.ex: He is ill and cannot go to school.
words.ex_cn: 他生病了，不能去上学。
words.en: If you are ill, you are suffering from a disease or a health problem.

words.ex: He stayed home because of illness.
words.ex_cn: 他因为生病待在家里。
words.en: An illness is a particular disease, especially one that is not very serious.

words.tr: adj. 更坏的；更糟糕的；“bad”的比较级； adv. 更糟；更坏；
words.ex: The weather got worse after noon.
words.ex_cn: 下午之后天气变得更坏了。
words.en: Comparative of bad : more unpleasant, difficult, or severe than before or than something else that is also bad

words.tr: v. 使留下深刻印象；使铭记；
words.ex: His speech impressed everyone in the room.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲给在场的每个人留下了深刻印象。
words.en: If someone or something impresses you, you feel great admiration for them.

words.ex: His smile left a good impression on me.
words.ex_cn: 他的微笑给我留下了好印象。
words.en: An idea, feeling, or opinion about something or someone, especially one formed without conscious thought or on the basis of little evidence.

words.tr: adj. 印象深刻的； v. 使印象深刻；“impress”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: I was impressed by her kindness.
words.ex_cn: 她的善良给我留下了深刻的印象。
words.en: If you are impressed by something or someone, you feel great admiration for them.

words.ex: His speech was very impressive.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲非常令人印象深刻。
words.en: Something that is impressive makes you admire it because it is very good, large, important, etc.

words.tr:
n. 种类；
adj. 善良的；和蔼的；
words.ex: There are many kinds of fruits in the market.
words.ex_cn: 市场上有各种各样的水果。
words.en: If you describe someone as kind, you mean that they are gentle, caring, and helpful.

words.ex: She kindly helped me with my homework.
words.ex_cn: 她亲切地帮我做作业。
words.en: If someone is kindly, they are friendly and behave in a gentle and caring way.

words.ex: Her kindness helped me when I was sad.
words.ex_cn: 当我不开心时，她的善意帮助了我。
words.en: Kindness is the quality of being gentle, caring, and helpful.

words.tr: phrase. 有点；稍微；有一点……的
words.ex: It was a little kind of boring, but okay.
words.ex_cn: 这有点无聊，但还好。

words.tr: phrase. 各种各样的；各种类型的
words.ex: He collects all kinds of stamps.
words.ex_cn: 他收集各种各样的邮票。
words.en: A phrase used to indicate a variety of different types or kinds of something.

words.tr:
v. 击；撞；
n. 撞击；敲击；
words.ex: He knock on the door.
words.ex_cn: 他敲了敲门。
words.en: To strike a surface noisily to attract attention, especially when waiting to be let in through a door.

words.tr: phrase. 打， 捶， 敲; 挝
words.ex: He knock at the door every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上敲门。
words.en: To strike a surface noisily to attract attention, especially when waiting to be let in through a door.

words.ex: He knocks on the door before entering.
words.ex_cn: 他进入前敲门。
words.en: To strike a door with the knuckles, a hard object, etc., in order to attract attention or gain entry.

words.ex: He speaks English as his first language.
words.ex_cn: 他说英语作为他的第一语言。
words.en: Language is the system of communication in speech and writing that is used by people of a particular country or area.

words.tr: phrase. 母语；本族语；第一语言
words.ex: She speaks her mother language at home.
words.ex_cn: 她在家里说她的母语。
words.en: The first language a person learns from birth, also known as a native language.

words.ex: He has a large house.
words.ex_cn: 他有一所大房子。
words.en: Something that is large is greater in size than usual or average.

words.ex: He is largely responsible for the project's success.
words.ex_cn: 他主要对这个项目的成功负责。
words.en: To a great extent; mostly.

words.ex: This box is larger than that one.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子比那个大。
words.en: Of considerable or great size or extent.

words.tr:
adj. 最后的；最近的；
v. 持续；
adv. 最后；最近一次；
words.ex: This is the last chance to pass the exam.
words.ex_cn: 这是通过考试的最后机会。
words.en: Coming after all others in time or order; final.

words.ex: The meeting will last for two hours.
words.ex_cn: 会议将持续两个小时。
words.en: To continue for a specific period of time.

words.tr:
adj. 晚的；迟的；已故的；
adv. 晚；迟；
words.ex: The train is late.
words.ex_cn: 火车晚点了。
words.en: After the expected, usual, or proper time.

words.ex: I haven't seen him lately.
words.ex_cn: 我最近没见到他。
words.en: If you say that something has happened lately, you mean that it has happened recently.

words.tr:
adv. 后来；稍后；
adj. 后来的；稍后的；晚些的；晚年的；
words.ex: He left the party, and later he called his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他离开了派对，后来给朋友打了电话。
words.en: Later means after the present time or after the time you are talking about.

words.tr:
v. 引导；领导；带头；
n. 主导地位；铅；领先；
words.ex: The teacher leads the students to the library.
words.ex_cn: 老师带领学生去图书馆。
words.en: To be in charge of a group, country, or situation; to guide or direct in a course; a position of advantage in a contest or competition; a heavy, malleable, ductile, bluish-white, dense metallic element.

words.tr: abbr. “light-emitting diode”的缩写；发光二级管；
words.ex: The streetlights use led bulbs to save energy.
words.ex_cn: 街灯使用LED灯泡来节省能源。
words.en: Led is the past tense and past participle of lead, which means to guide or direct in a course.

words.ex: He is a leader who helps his team succeed.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位帮助团队取得成功的领袖。
words.en: A leader is the person in charge of a group, organization, or country, who makes decisions and ensures that things are done effectively.

words.ex: Can you lend me your pen?
words.ex_cn: 你能把你的笔借给我吗？
words.en: If you lend something you own to someone else, you allow them to have it or use it for a period of time, after which they must return it to you.

words.tr: v. 借给；“lend”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: I lent my book to my friend.
words.ex_cn: 我把我的书借给了我的朋友。
words.en: The past tense and past participle of lend, meaning to give something to someone for a period of time, expecting that it will be returned.

words.ex: I have math lesson every Monday.
words.ex_cn: 我每周一都有数学课。
words.en: A lesson is a period of time in which someone is taught about a particular subject or how to do something.

words.ex: I learn a lesson from my failure.
words.ex_cn: 我从失败中吸取教训。

words.tr:
v. 举起；提起；抬起；
n. 电梯；搭便车；
words.ex: He lift the box with both hands.
words.ex_cn: 他用双手举起箱子。
words.en: To lift something means to move it to a higher position. A lift is a device that carries people or goods up and down inside buildings.

words.tr: phrase. 举起；抬起；鼓舞；使振奋
words.ex: He lift up the box with both hands.
words.ex_cn: 他用双手把箱子举起来。
words.en: to raise something or someone to a higher position or level

words.tr:
n. 光；灯；光线；
adj. 轻的；浅的；少量的；明亮的；
v. 点燃；照亮；
words.ex: The light from the window brightened the room.
words.ex_cn: 窗户透进来的光让房间变亮了。
words.en: Light is the natural agent that stimulates sight and makes things visible. It is also used to describe something that is not heavy or a source of illumination.

words.tr: v. 点燃；照亮；“light”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He lit the candle with a match.
words.ex_cn: 他用火柴点燃了蜡烛。
words.en: Past tense and past participle of 'light', meaning to ignite or to illuminate.

words.tr: v. 点燃；照亮；“light”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The lamp was lighted by the child.
words.ex_cn: 灯被孩子点亮了。
words.en: To make something start burning; to provide light for a place.

words.ex: The candles light up the room.
words.ex_cn: 蜡烛点亮了房间。
words.en: To make something bright or to start to burn.

words.ex: He drew a straight line on the paper.
words.ex_cn: 他在纸上画了一条直线。
words.en: A line is a long thin mark which is drawn or painted on a surface.

words.ex: He waits in line for the bus every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上排队等公交车。
words.en: To stand in a line and wait for one's turn.

words.tr: phrase. 插队；不按顺序加入行列
words.ex: He cut in line at the grocery store.
words.ex_cn: 他在杂货店插队。
words.en: To move ahead of others who are waiting in line, in a way that is considered rude or unfair.

words.ex: There is little water left in the bottle.
words.ex_cn: 瓶子里剩下的水很少。
words.en: Small in size, amount, or degree (often used to convey an appealing diminutiveness or express an affectionate or dismissive attitude).

words.tr: adv. 较少地；更少地；“little”的比较级； adj. 更少的；“little”的比较级； pron. 较少；更少；
words.ex: He eats less sugar now.
words.ex_cn: 他现在吃得更少的糖。
words.en: You use less to indicate that there is a smaller amount of something than before or than average. You can use 'less' to indicate that something is smaller in size or degree than another thing.

words.tr:
adv. 最小；最少；
adj. 最少的；最小的；
n. 最小；最少；
words.ex: He ran the least among all the runners.
words.ex_cn: 他在所有跑步者中跑得最少。
words.en: You use least to indicate that something is the smallest in amount, degree, or size, or the lowest in importance.

words.tr: adj. 孤独的；寂寞的；偏僻的；
words.ex: He felt lonely after his dog died.
words.ex_cn: 他的狗去世后，他感到孤独。
words.en: If you are lonely, you are unhappy because you are alone or do not have anyone you can talk to.

words.ex: He felt loneliness after moving to a new city.
words.ex_cn: 他搬到新城市后感到孤独。
words.en: Loneliness is the unhappiness that is felt by someone because they do not have any friends or do not have anyone to talk to.

words.ex: He won the lottery by pure luck.
words.ex_cn: 他纯粹是靠运气中了彩票。
words.en: Luck is the force that causes things, especially good things, to happen to you by chance and not as a result of your own efforts or abilities.

words.ex: He is lucky to win the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他很幸运赢得了奖品。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as lucky, you mean that they have something which is very desirable or that they are in a very desirable situation.

words.ex: He is unlucky because he lost his wallet.
words.ex_cn: 他很倒霉，因为他丢了钱包。
words.en: If someone is unlucky, they have bad luck.

words.ex: Luckily, the bus came just in time.
words.ex_cn: 幸运的是，公交车正好及时到了。
words.en: You use luckily to indicate that something good has happened because of chance or luck, rather than because of someone's skill or planning.

words.ex: Unluckily, he missed the bus this morning.
words.ex_cn: 不幸的是，他今天早上错过了公交车。
words.en: In an unfortunate or unlucky manner.

words.ex: They will marry next summer.
words.ex_cn: 他们将在明年夏天结婚。
words.en: To marry someone means to become their husband or wife in a legal or religious ceremony.

words.ex: Their marriage lasted for twenty years.
words.ex_cn: 他们的婚姻持续了二十年。
words.en: The legally or formally recognized union of two people as partners in a personal relationship.

words.ex: He wants to marry his girlfriend next year.
words.ex_cn: 他想明年和女朋友结婚。
words.en: To become the husband or wife of someone.

words.ex: She got married to him last year.
words.ex_cn: 她去年嫁给了他。

words.tr:
v. 相配；
n. 比赛；
words.ex: The curtains match the sofa.
words.ex_cn: 窗帘和沙发相配。
words.en: A match is a competition or game in which people or teams compete against each other. It can also refer to a small stick that produces a flame when rubbed against a rough surface, used for lighting a fire, cigarette, etc. Additionally, it can mean a person or thing that is equal to another in quality, strength, or suitability.

words.tr: phrase. 与…匹配；与…相配；使与…一致
words.ex: The curtains don't match with the paint color.
words.ex_cn: 窗帘与油漆的颜色不搭配。
words.en: To be compatible or suitable with something or someone.

words.tr:
n. 事情；物质；
v. 要紧；
words.ex: What's the matter with you?
words.ex_cn: 你怎么了？
words.en: Matter is a physical substance in general, as distinct from mind and spirit; (in physics) that which occupies space and possesses rest mass, especially as distinct from energy. It can also refer to a subject or situation under consideration.

words.tr: phrase. 没关系；无所谓；不重要
words.ex: It doesn't matter if you're late, just come when you can.
words.ex_cn: phrase. 如果你迟到也没关系，能来的时候来就行。
words.en: Used to say that something is not important or that you should not worry about it.

words.tr:
n. 头脑；意向；心；智力；
v. 介意；注意；
words.ex: He lost his mind after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故后失去了理智。
words.en: Your mind is your ability to think and reason. If you mind something, you are bothered by it or you object to it.

words.tr: phrase. 介意做某事；反对做某事
words.ex: Would you mind doing your homework now?
words.ex_cn: 你介意现在做作业吗？
words.en: To be willing to do something or to have no objection to doing something.

words.ex: The mouse ran under the table.
words.ex_cn: 老鼠跑到了桌子下面。
words.en: A mouse is a small animal with a long tail, which is found in houses and fields and is often kept as a pet. In computing, a mouse is a small device that you move across a surface in order to move a cursor on your computer screen.

words.ex: The cats chased the mice in the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 猫在厨房里追老鼠。
words.en: Mice are small rodents that are typically characterized by a pointed snout, small rounded ears, a body-length scaly tail, and a high breeding rate.

words.tr:
n. 姓名；名称；
v. 说出…的名字；命名；
words.ex: His name is Tom.
words.ex_cn: 他的名字是汤姆。
words.en: The word or words that a person, thing, or place is known by.

words.ex: The park was named after a famous hero.
words.ex_cn: 这个公园是以一位著名英雄的名字命名的。
words.en: If you name someone or something after another person or thing, you give them the same name as that person or thing.

words.ex: The nation celebrated its independence day.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家庆祝了它的独立日。
words.en: A nation is a country considered as a group of people with the same language, culture, and history, who live in a particular area under one government.

words.ex: The national flag flies high every morning.
words.ex_cn: 每天早上国旗都高高飘扬。
words.en: relating to or characteristic of a nation; common to a whole nation

words.tr:
adj. 本土的；
n. 土著；本地人；
words.ex: This plant is native to Australia.
words.ex_cn: 这种植物原产于澳大利亚。
words.en: A native of a particular country or region is someone who was born in that country or region.

words.ex: He speaks his native language at home.
words.ex_cn: 他在家说他的本地话。
words.en: A native language is the first language that a person learns to speak when they are a baby, rather than a language learned at school or as an adult.

words.tr: phrase. 就其本质而言；天生地
words.ex: He is by nature a quiet person.
words.ex_cn: 他天性安静。
words.en: If someone has a particular quality by nature, they have it as a natural part of their character.

words.tr:
adv. 两者都不；
adj. 两者都不的；
conj. 也不；
pron. 两者都不；
words.ex: I don't like coffee, and neither do I like tea.
words.ex_cn: 我不喜欢咖啡，也不喜欢茶。
words.en: used to introduce a further negative statement after a negative one, or to indicate that a negative statement is also true of another person or thing

words.ex: Neither Tom nor Anna likes coffee.
words.ex_cn: 汤姆和安娜都不喜欢咖啡。
words.en: You use neither...nor when you are talking about two or more things that are not true or that do not happen.
